articles.title: Cubs Set Team Record With Historic Unanswered Run Streak Over Last 3 Games
articles.summary: The Chicago Cubs set a franchise record this week by scoring 30 unanswered runs, per Sarah Langs of MLB.com.
articles.body:
The Chicago Cubs set a franchise record this week by scoring 30 unanswered runs, per Sarah Langs of MLB.com.

The Cubs got the job done over a three-game stretch this week.

Chicago scored 19 runs in the final seven innings of a 19-2 road win over the Seattle Mariners on Sunday, including five in the third and nine in the ninth. Ian Happ and Pedro Ramirez each hit homers and drove in five runs.

The Cubs then headed to Arizona and shut out the Diamondbacks 7-0 on Monday, with Michael Conforto leading the way thanks to a homer on a 3-for-3 day.

Chicago then scored the first four runs against the Diamondbacks on Tuesday, with Happ's three-run homer starting that effort. However, Arizona scored three in the eighth and two in the ninth for the 5-4 comeback win.

The record for most unanswered runs in a game during the modern era (dating back to 1901) is 30 , set by the Texas Rangers on Aug. 22, 2007 against the Baltimore Orioles in a 30-3 win (that is also the mark for the most runs scored in a single game in the modern era as well).

The Pittsburgh Pirates notably scored 37 consecutive runs over a seven-game span in June 1903 that also included six shutouts.

In the present date, the 76-57 Cubs lead the major leagues with 695 runs. They sit second in the NL Central, 5.5 games back of the Milwaukee Brewers.

Chicago will finish its three-game set with Arizona on Wednesday before heading home to host the Cincinnati Reds for three more contests beginning Friday.

articles.title: Brewers Manager Calls Out Cooper Pratt After Benching For Lack of Hustle In Loss to Mets
articles.summary: Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy explained why he pulled rookie shortstop Cooper Pratt from the game during the fifth inning of Tuesday's 3-2 loss to the New York Mets.
articles.body:
Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy explained why he pulled rookie shortstop Cooper Pratt from the game during the fifth inning of Tuesday's 3-2 loss to the New York Mets.

Murphy told reporters after the game that he made the decision to take Pratt out of the game in favor of David Hamilton after he only managed a single on a pop-up that landed in between three Mets fielders in shallow right field in the fifth inning.

"He popped a ball up to right field and didn't run, and the ball landed and stopped," Murphy said. "He would've easily got to second base. What could've happened after that, I'm not sure, but you can't have a guy not understanding that."

Murphy added, "You've got to be locked in if you're going to play at this level. ... You'd better run."

Meanwhile, Pratt acknowledged that he should have been hustling out of the batter's box rather than watching to see if the ball would fall in, saying, "There is no excuse. I should've ran hard no matter if it's foul or fair, if it's an out. I should've been busting my butt to get to second base. Some of the guys pulled me aside and let me know, 'Hey, this is how we do it here,' and I know that. It won't happen again."

Murphy suggested that pulling Pratt from the game was the result of multiple issues rather than just his inability to get to second base on the fifth-inning pop-up.

The reigning two-time National League Manager of the Year told reporters that Pratt not getting a bunt down in the third inning also factored into his decision, saying, "We asked him to get a bunt down, pulled back on a strike, and that happens, maybe. Trying to get a guy second and third for [Jackson] Chourio in a game where we weren't swinging it too good."

Milwaukee did not get a run in during the third or fifth innings, and they went on to lose 3-2 to the Mets in 10 innings.

At 81-51, the Brewers have the best record in Major League Baseball, and much of that is thanks to their ability to effectively play small ball when needed.

Pratt didn't execute in those situations on Tuesday, but Murphy noted that he still has confidence in the 22-year-old rookie, saying, "I love the kid, and I believe in the kid immensely. He's got to be a player that does those things. He's not going to hit 30 homers at this point in his career. He's a great defender and a really capable offensive player, and we can't have that."

The Brewers will return to action Wednesday night against the Mets before finishing up the series on Thursday night.

articles.title: Kwanza Jones Becomes First Black Woman Majority Owner Of An MLB Team In $3.9B San Diego Padres Deal
articles.summary: Kwanza Jones has made history with her investment in baseball.
articles.body:
Kwanza Jones has made history with her investment in baseball.

Jones and her husband José E. Feliciano are the new owners of the Padres, per the MLB.

Investing in the team was a no-brainer for the couple. As AFROTECH

previously reported, the Seidler family agreed to sell the Padres to Jones and Feliciano in a deal reportedly valued at $3.9 billion. This makes Jones the first Black woman to own an MLB team.

She sits on various boards, including UCLA Health and the Apollo Theatre, has been investing for more than a decade, and is a Princeton University graduate, as is her husband.

The pair were unanimously approved by the league and its owners to become the new owners of the Padres on Aug. 17, according to a press release. By Aug. 24, they had received an official welcome.

They own nearly a 45% stake in the team through their "personal investment," Sports Business Journal reports.

"We are a family first, and becoming owners of the San Diego Padres means joining an even larger one," Jones and Feliciano said in the press release. "We have built our life and our work together, and we will bring that same shared purpose, commitment, and determination to our stewardship of the Padres. It is a source of immense pride and an extraordinary opportunity to become part of a team, a tradition, and the San Diego community that has supported it so faithfully."

"Our ambition is clear: to bring a World Series championship to San Diego and build an enduring organization capable of competing for championships year after year. We intend to be engaged owners, bringing our energy, experience, and perspective while working alongside the talented team already in place and investing ambitiously and thoughtfully in the Padres' future. That means pursuing excellence and innovation throughout the organization, delivering a first-class experience at Petco Park, deepening the bond with the faithful fans, and making a positive impact across the San Diego community. We are all in and committed to winning," they continued.

articles.title: UL Lafayette seeks to name baseball complex to honor Tony Robichaux
articles.summary: LAFAYETTE, LA. (KLFY) — The University of Louisiana at Lafayette is seeking approval to name its baseball complex Tony Robichaux Park in honor of the winning...
articles.body:
LAFAYETTE, LA. ( KLFY ) -- The University of Louisiana at Lafayette is seeking approval to name its baseball complex Tony Robichaux Park in honor of the winningest baseball coach in Louisiana collegiate history. UL Lafayette also is asking the University of Louisiana System Board of Supervisors to name its baseball stadium club for the Russo family, longtime supporters of Ragin' Cajuns Athletics.

The board will consider both proposals during a meeting on Thursday.

Chris J. Russo has pledged $1.225 million for the philanthropic naming of the Russo Stadium Club in honor of his family. He has committed an additional $500,000 to seed the Friends of Tony Robichaux Fund, which will support the baseball program and launch a $5 million fundraising campaign.

Russo said the gifts honor two legacies that have shaped his family's relationship with the University: his father, the late Samuel "Sammy Joe" J. Russo Sr., whose love of Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns Baseball became a family tradition, and Coach Robichaux, whose influence reached throughout the program and community.

"My father and I shared many special moments watching the Cajuns play, and supporting this program has always meant a great deal to our family," Russo said. "Naming the stadium club for the Russo family honors those memories. Helping create Tony Robichaux Park and launching the Friends of Tony Robichaux Fund honors a coach whose impact reached far beyond baseball. We are proud to help preserve his legacy and strengthen the program he loved."

[sailthru_widget name="Sailthru Widget Block" sailthru_list="Daily News" title="KLFY Daily Digest"]

Robichaux won 1,177 games during a 33-year career at McNeese State and at Louisiana. He remains the only coach in NCAA history to become the career wins leader at two Division I programs in the same state.

During 25 seasons with the Ragin' Cajuns from 1995 to 2019, Robichaux won 914 games and led the team to 12 NCAA Regional appearances, four Super Regionals and the 2000 College World Series, where they finished tied for third nationally. His 2014 team finished 58-10, earned the program's first No. 1 national ranking and recorded an .853 winning percentage that remains among the best in NCAA history.

Trey Frazier, UL's interim athletics director, shared how naming the stadium after Coach Robichaux would be a trmendous honor to his legacy.

"The opportunity to place the name of the man who envisioned this stadium and, more importantly, touched the lives of hundreds of young men who came through this program is a tremendous honor and privilege," Frazier said. "Coach Robichaux's legacy is that of a true servant leader and teacher who used the game of baseball to prepare his players for the game of life. His passion for this University, his love for his family and his players, and his unwavering devotion to the Ragin' Cajuns fanbase are qualities we will carry forward for generations to come."

Robichaux's teams won seven Sun Belt Conference regular-season championships and four conference tournament championships. He coached 29 All-Americans and five Academic All-Americans, and 67 Ragin' Cajuns were selected in the Major League Baseball Draft during his tenure.

His influence extended far beyond his record. He built Louisiana Baseball into a nationally respected program while emphasizing servant leadership and the development of young men as leaders, husbands and fathers. He also helped transform M.L. "Tigue" Moore Field into one of the nation's premier on-campus baseball facilities.

"Coach Robichaux taught generations of young men that baseball was never only about winning games. It was about discipline, accountability, faith and service," said University President Dr. Ramesh Kolluru. "Tony Robichaux Park will ensure that the place he helped build carries forward the values he lived and the standard he set. We are deeply grateful to Chris Russo and the entire Russo family for helping make this tribute possible and for investing in the next generation of Louisiana Baseball."

A native of Crowley, Tony Robichaux died July 3, 2019, at age 57. He was inducted into the McNeese Athletics Hall of Fame in 2017, the UL Lafayette Athletics Hall of Fame in 2021, the American Baseball Coaches Hall of Fame in 2021 and the Louisiana Sports Hall of Fame in 2022.

"Nobody embodied Cajuns Baseball for more than 25 years than Coach Tony Robichaux," current Louisiana head baseball coach Matt Deggs said. "When I see his name up there, it will feel like home. I'll think about all the history and memories, and all the blood, sweat and tears he poured into this program. It's coming full circle, and while it's a huge moment for our program, it's an even bigger honor for the Robichaux family."

articles.title: Yankees Executive Announced for 'Survivor' Season 51 Cast Ahead of Sept. 23 Premiere
articles.summary: The World Series championship isn't the only title New York Yankees assistant director of baseball operations Mike Pinsky will compete for this fall.
articles.body:
The World Series championship isn't the only title New York Yankees assistant director of baseball operations Mike Pinsky will compete for this fall.

Terry Terrones of The Hollywood Reporter relayed the full 21-person cast for the 51st season of CBS' hit show Survivor on Wednesday, and Pinsky is included.

Survivor returns Sept. 23 with the premiere of what is being described as its "Open Era." Terrones noted host Jeff Probst said that means, "Anything that's ever happened on Survivor can happen again—at any time, in any order, without warning."

In Pinsky's profile for the show, he uses "enthusiastic, strategic, driven" when asked for three words to describe him. He also said he has been a devoted fan of the show for decades and even played Survivor with his friends when he was eight years old.

"When I was 28, my marriage proposal to my wife Becky incorporated a Probst catchphrase," Pinsky continued. "Getting to actually live this dream for real is a one-of-one life experience, and the thrill of this type of adventure sets my heart on fire!"

The 32-year-old has been with the Yankees in some role since January 2017 and was promoted to assistant director of baseball operations in 2022.

Now he can add Survivor contestant to that baseball-filled resume.

articles.title: Joey, Jesse Buss join new Padres ownership group, reportedly strike deal to acquire approximately 5% of club
articles.summary: Through their new investment group, Buss Sports Capital, the Buss brothers are also pursuing an NBA Europe ownership stake, according to multiple reports.
articles.body:
Joey and Jesse Buss, the youngest sons of former Los Angeles Lakers owner Dr. Jerry Buss , announced Wednesday that through the investment group they founded, Buss Sports Capital, they have joined the new San Diego Padres ownership group fronted by the husband-wife tandem of José E. Feliciano and Kwanza Jones.

Buss Sports Capital, according to multiple reports , has struck a deal to acquire approximately 5% of the Padres, whose sale to Feliciano and Jones was unanimously approved by MLB owners on Aug. 17 .

Feliciano and Jones spearheaded the reported $3.9 billion purchase, which ranks among the most expensive franchise sales in North American sports history . That list is headlined by not one but two sales of the Los Angeles Lakers, whom Los Angeles Dodgers owner Mark Walter just agreed to sell to an ownership group led by businessmen Josh Kushner and Bob Iger for a record $12.5 billion .

Not long after Walter began his brief Lakers ownership stint, Joey and Jesse Buss were relieved of their front-office duties with the organization . Soon enough came the inception of Buss Sports Capital, which, according to both ESPN and The Athletic , is also pursuing an NBA Europe ownership stake , even after investing in the Padres.

Joey and Jesse Buss announced, per ESPN's report , that they will serve on the Padres ownership group's advisory board.

While with the Lakers, Joey Buss served as the franchise's alternate governor and vice president of research and development. Jesse Buss, meanwhile, occupied the roles of assistant general manager and director of scouting.

"We are honored to join Kwanza and José and have the opportunity to contribute to the future of a team that Jesse and I have loved since we were kids growing up in San Diego," Joey Buss said in a statement, via ESPN. "Sports have always been a part of our family's story, and great organizations have a unique ability to bring people together and create a lasting sense of community. Padres fans have built one of the most passionate and loyal communities in all of sports, and we believe there is a tremendous opportunity to deepen that connection in San Diego and around the world. "The Padres are on the cusp of something special, and through Buss Sports Capital, we look forward to bringing our experience and perspective to the ownership group and doing our part to build on the strong foundation already in place." Jesse Buss added in a statement, per ESPN: "Joey and I had the privilege of learning from our father and then spending nearly two decades building our own careers in professional basketball operations. We saw firsthand what it takes to build a championship organization, and throughout our careers have applied those lessons across talent evaluation, roster construction, player development and long-term organizational planning. While every sport is different, we believe the principles behind building sustained success are universal."

Following the news of Walter's impending sale of the Lakers to Kushner and Iger, an agreement reportedly concerning only Walter's shares in the franchise , five Buss siblings — Johnny, Jimmy, Janie, Joey and Jesse — announced their intent to sell the family's remaining 17.8% ownership stake in the Lakers .

Their sister, Jeanie Buss, whose title of Lakers governor will be jeopardized with that sale, is contesting it through her lawyer .

articles.body: 'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday–Friday on OutKick.com. Final Hump Day of August. Seriously. Weren't we just doing this in July? And now, we're six days away from September. Lordy. Be careful. You blink, and it'll be Halloween. Blink again, and we'll be rocking around the Christmas tree. Summer goes by faster and faster each year, doesn't it? As you get older, you really do understand what your grandparents meant when they said "it goes by faster each year." My grandma used to say that all the time. I rolled my eyes. Not anymore. We're 72 hours away from kickoff in Dublin. Red Sox-Yanks this weekend in the Bronx for what is essentially a playoff series to decide who hosts who in October. I'll be in Daytona for the Firecracker 400. Summer is certainly going out with a bang. Let's finish strong. Welcome to a Hump Day Nightcaps — the one where little leaguer Kinley Rasmus throws her hat in the ring for greatest LLWS player of all time. LITTLE LEAGUE TEAM GETS ABSOLUTELY SCREWED ON FINAL PITCH OF NO-HITTER, FANS STUNNED BY CALL Seriously. This girl is insane. Wait till you see her bloodline, too. What else? I've got a beaten and battered Caitlin Clark, new CBS college football sideline reporter Jordan Giorgio reporting for duty ahead of Week 1, and this sports question is getting a lot of traction over on Elon's X today. Feels right in our wheelhouse. You'll see. OK, grab you a drink, pour it out for Tim Curry, and then settle in for a Hump Day 'Cap! Kinley Rasmus is an absolute machine on the diamond Goodness, what a week. First Dolly, now Tim. Brutal. And how about the year for Home Alone II cast members? We lost Catherine O'Hara in January. We lost Brenda Fricker — AKA the Pigeon Lady — last month. And now we lose Tim Curry. Obviously, Tim is most well-known (I think?) for his work in "Rocky Horror Picture Show," but, for me, he's the hotel manager in Home Alone II. Other notable roles for Tim? How about the original IT? Terrifying movie for us '90s kids to walk past in the horror section at Blockbuster Video. It gave me nightmares for WEEKS. And how about this for a real deep cut? He was also the voice of Ben Ravencroft in the cult classic, "Scooby-Doo! and the Witch's Ghost." If you knew that, you get a gold star for today's class. Extra credit! Anyway, we lost a good one in Tim. We lost a good one in Dolly. We're losing too many good ones right now. Not great. OK, let's get this class started with Little League World Series star, Kinley Rasmus, who last night became the record-holder for most hits in the LLWS (5) for a girl, and also tied the all-time LLWS record for strikeouts by a girl (14), set by Mo’ne Davis. What a phenom: Caitlin Clark looks like she's having fun! Amazing. I can't get enough of this story. I'm a sucker for a good LLWS story, and Kinley checks all the right boxes. And how about this family tree: Not a bad little family tree! Kinley, 12, is currently 5 for 8 in four LLWS games, and has 14 Ks in two starts. There's a lot of talk right now about girls and guys (and ... others ...) playing in sports, and the fairness of it all. It's well documented. Sophie Cunningham. Ever heard of her?! Of course you have. This is a nice way to veer off that path and cleanse the palette with something genuine. We all need it. Trust me. I'm so tired of the WNBA stuff. It's why I led with Kinley today. She deserves it. Phenix City Little League (Alabama) plays again tonight at 7 p.m., for those looking to kill time before college football returns on Saturday. OK, let's keep this class moving ... with the WNBA! Yes, that league. I know it's exhausting, but when Caitlin Clark emerges from a game looking like she just got clawed to death, I have to report on it: Worst sports moments ever & it's time to report for duty! Lordy. Look at her! Just beaten and battered, and she still managed to put up 37 points. Look, it's basketball. I get it. I'm not here trying to sound soft or whiny. Sports are violent. They're physical. I'd imagine the '80s and '90s Bulls and Pistons looked a lot like this after games. I assume a lot of players who went up against the Pistons back then did. I get it. Now, replace the Bad Boy Pistons with the Mean Girls in the WNBA, and give them all fingernails and enough hate in their hearts to fill an ocean. That's what Caitlin is going up against every night. They really do hate her. It's amazing. OK, let's rapid-fire this Hump Day class into a big Hump Day night. First up? This sports question has gone mega-viral on Elon's X today, and it's perfect for this group: "oh yeah you like sports? name five times your team has made you want to ...." You know the rest. I'm not going to finish the post here for legal reasons. But you get the question. It's a great topic because everyone has answers that immediately come to mind. For me? It's a weird list, admittedly, but it's a solid one in terms of heartbreak. I'd also throw in Tim Tebow getting absolutely boat-raced by Alabama in his final SEC championship game in 2009. That one hurt, too. OK, shoot me yours. I know we're all sickos here, so I'm expecting a full mailbox tomorrow morning. STAY "FEARLESS" ON THE GO! TAKE TOMI LAHREN WITH YOU. articles.title: ESPN’s Little League Classic outdraws Netflix’s Field of Dreams
articles.summary: ESPN scored a season-high audience for its presentation of the MLB Little League Classic while also averaging more viewers than MLB at Field of Dreams game o...
articles.body:
ESPN scored a season-high audience for its presentation of the MLB Little League Classic while also averaging more viewers than MLB at Field of Dreams game on Netflix. However, the viewership still fell below NBC's Sunday Night Baseball average.

Sunday's Atlanta Braves - Milwaukee Brewers game in the Little League Classic averaged 2 million viewers across ESPN and ESPN2. Viewership was up 19% from Seattle Mariners-New York Mets in last year's edition (1.70 million).

The game was also ESPN play-by-play man Karl Ravech's final MLB assignment for ESPN after he was laid off by the network.

Viewership peaked at 2.2 million viewers during the 9:45 p.m. ET quarter-hour. It was the most-watched MLB broadcast of the year on ESPN and the second-most-watched Little League Classic ever, behind New York Yankees-Detroit Tigers in 2024 (2.2 million).

ESPN's previous most-watched broadcast was St. Louis Cardinals-Chicago Cubs last weekend on ABC, which averaged 1.99 million.

The Little League Classic also easily surpassed the viewership of MLB at Field of Dreams on Netflix ( 1.66 million) . That is a stark contrast from the two other MLB at Field of Dreams events in 2021 and 2022, which both aired on Fox. In 2021, Fox averaged 5.87 million for Field of Dreams compared to 1.01 million for the Little League Classic on ESPN. The next season, Field of Dreams averaged 3.10 million, while the Little League Classic did 1.18 million on ESPN.

Despite the strong numbers for ESPN, the broadcast was not the most-watched MLB telecast of the week. Baseball Night in America on Fox averaged 3.08 million for regional action Saturday night, featuring Giants- Red Sox , Pirates-Dodgers and Cubs-Mariners. That is the third-most-watched Baseball Night in America window this season. Overall, MLB games on Fox are averaging 2.40 million viewers, up 19% from last year.

ESPN's Little League Classic broadcast aired in the network's old Sunday Night Baseball window. Starting this season, that primetime window moved to NBC. The Little League Classic fared less well when compared to Sunday Night Baseball viewership. This season, primetime Sunday Night Baseball games have averaged 2.49 million viewers on NBC and 2.75 million viewers when including Peacock streaming viewership measured by Adobe Analytics.

San Francisco Giants-Boston Red Sox, which aired Sunday afternoon on NBC and Peacock, averaged 1.7 million viewers. That is tied for the lowest audience of the season on the network with Rangers-Red Sox on Sunday, June 14.

Looking ahead, the Little League Classic will not be on a Sunday next season. Major League Baseball announced that the game will be played on Thursday, August 19, next year, and will feature the Chicago Cubs and Toronto Blue Jays .

articles.title: Diamondbacks manager Torey Lovullo apologizes to Chicago Cubs after sign stealing controversy: 'bush league'
articles.summary: Torey Lovullo apologized to Craig Counsell after the league confirmed Cubs third base coach Quintin Berry's sign stealing was perfectly legal.
articles.body: It's one of baseball's oldest, and often most misunderstood, traditions: stealing signs from the opposition. Despite popular misconceptions, sign stealing in baseball is perfectly legal. If, say, a runner at second base is able to pick up signs from the catcher to the pitcher, he's within his rights to relay them to the hitter. It's up to the pitcher and catcher to come up with their own elaborate system to keep the other team guessing. The Houston Astros in 2017 and into 2018 are the most obvious and prominent example of how sign stealing could be abused, particularly in the pre-pitchcom era. Should players or coaches pick up on signs and relay them on the field, there's no issue. However, when teams employ video technology to relay signs in real time from the dugout, as the Astros did, that crosses into cheating. articles.title: Yankees place Fernando Cruz on IL, add Michael Fulmer with bullpen in desperate shape
articles.summary: As reporters waited for Fernando Cruz after the Yankees’ loss to the Astros on Tuesday, the struggling reliever exited the Bombers’ clubhouse with team train...
articles.body:
As reporters waited for Fernando Cruz after the Yankees ' loss to the Astros on Tuesday, the struggling reliever exited the Bombers' clubhouse with team trainer Tim Lentych. Aaron Boone waited for the duo at the back of the room, and Cruz then debriefed with a club spokesperson immediately before telling reporters that he felt healthy.

"Yeah, I'm feeling good," the right-hander said Tuesday night. "I mean, every player has the battles with their bodies and stuff, but we're gonna be good."

And yet, after the atypical postgame scene the night before , it wasn't surprising to see Cruz placed on the 15-day injured list with right elbow discomfort before Wednesday's game against Houston .

The Yankees made several other moves before the game, adding newly-signed reliever Michael Fulmer to the active roster; recalling the evening's starting pitcher, Elmer Rodríguez; and optioning reliever Bradley Hanner. Kervin Castro , another reliever, was also transferred to the 60-day IL.

On Wednesday afternoon, Boone said that Cruz had gone through testing and imaging since Tuesday night. While the Yankees were still waiting on results, the team's training staff felt it was necessary to place Cruz on the IL, the manager said. Boone added that Cruz felt something on one of his pitches on Tuesday and alerted staffers.

Cruz, whose signature splitter has seen a drop-off in swing-and-miss, owns a 5.93 ERA and has allowed five home runs over his last 13.2 innings. That includes the game-tying, two-run shot he surrendered to Jeremy Peña on Tuesday.

Afterward, Cruz, who has also suffered a dip in velocity this season, said that he altered his mechanics a bit recently. He also downplayed the idea that fatigue has been an issue for a pitcher who has already surpassed his 2025 workload. With 54.2 innings pitched, Cruz has topped his total from a season ago. His 61 appearances, meanwhile, ranked 12th in the majors entering play on Wednesday.

(Brent Headrick's 68 games ranked second, highlighting just how much the Yankees have leaned on their top relievers.)

Cruz set career-highs with 69 games and 66.2 innings as a Red in 2024, but he didn't complain about his usage on Tuesday.

"I cannot control how many times I've been [used]," he said. "I'm just the guy that grabs the ball whenever it's needed, and I just go out there and compete."

On Wednesday, Boone didn't want to speculate whether Cruz's mechanical tweaks led to his IL stint, but he did say that fatigue is "always a factor" this time of year.

The Yankees, who did not acquire bullpen help of any kind , let alone the high-leverage variety, before the trade deadline, will have to hope that Cruz can get healthy and return to form before season's end. Prior to his scuffles, he had been the team's fireman, posting a 2.08 ERA over his first 34.2 innings this season.

In the meantime, the Yankees will have to rely on a few journeyman relievers, including Fulmer and Justin Topa , who was also signed recently. Boone said that they could find themselves in leverage situations with the Yankees' bullpen desperate and short on sure things.

"They're probably going to jump in the deep end," the skipper said.

Fulmer, who beat out ex-Yankee Gary Sánchez for the American League Rookie of the Year Award back in 2016, was recently designated for assignment by the Angels. He has a small recent big league sample, as he's only thrown 9.1 innings in The Show over the last two seasons. That includes 3.2 scoreless innings with the Angels this year.

The 33-year-old righty has had success in the Triple-A Pacific Coast League this season, recording a 2.93 ERA over 43 frames.

"Hopefully, he can come here and grab a role," Boone said. "There's opportunity there."

Fulmer said that the Yankees were the first team to reach out once he cleared waivers. He initially signed a minor league deal with them and planned on going to Triple-A on Tuesday night, but the team called about an hour after the ink dried and said that they needed him in the Bronx right away. A layover at LaGuardia — he was originally going to meet the RailRiders in Worcester, Massachusetts — ended up being his final destination, and he was dressed in full pinstripes just in time for the Yankees' photo day on Wednesday.

"I'm grateful to be with such a historic organization and grateful to be here right now," Fulmer said. "They said they were short in the bullpen a little bit and asked if I was ready to go tonight, and I said, 'Absolutely.'"

Fulmer, a starting pitcher at the onset of his career, noted that the Yankees are his seventh organization in the last two years. He and his wife have talked about retirement since Fulmer underwent his second Tommy John surgery in 2023, but his recent good health has motivated him to keep going.

Now the former Mets prospect is looking to lock down that role that Boone spoke of.

"I told [my wife] I couldn't live with myself feeling this healthy and throwing the ball this well to give up quite yet," Fulmer said. "So hopefully this is an opportunity for something in the long run. I'm just gonna compete my butt off."

Fulmer is not the only pitcher on the fringes trying to secure a spot in the Yankees' bullpen.

Again, there's Topa, and veteran Eli Morgan was also recently signed to a minor league deal.

Angel Chivilli (bone spur) entered the fourth day of his throwing program on Wednesday and can still be an option this season, Boone said. There is also Clarke Schmidt (Tommy John surgery), who is ready to begin a rehab assignment soon , and Luis Gil (shoulder), who has been at Triple-A. Both have been big league starters but are building up as relievers.

"He has a real chance to be a real factor for us in the pen," Boone said of Schmidt.

As for Gil, Boone said, "It seems like his build-up has gone well. I feel like his strike-throwing's well. The outings I've seen, it looks like the fastball is playing. So we've been encouraged with what we've seen so far."

The Yankees could also get Ryan Weathers back from a flexor strain before season's end; the southpaw would also slot into the bullpen. Meanwhile, Max Fried could be back in the Yankees' rotation this weekend if his bullpen session goes well on Thursday.

"We've definitely had some attrition here and gotten dinged a little bit on the injury front, but I feel like we're still very much in line to be really good at the very end when it matters the most, and even now down the stretch," Boone said. "So there's a couple spots semi-up for grabs now with some guys going down and some opportunities created, but hopefully we get Max back here on the weekend, and hopefully a couple guys can step up in bullpen roles to fortify that group that's obviously been so good for us all year."

One pitcher who no longer appears to be an option for the Yankees is Castro, who has been out with elbow neuritis. He has an upcoming appointment with Dr. Keith Meister, and surgery could be a possibility, Boone said.

articles.title: Jeanie Buss reportedly petitions court to block siblings' sale of Lakers stake, remove them as family trustees
articles.summary: The five other Buss siblings announced their intention to sell their Lakers stake last week.
articles.body:
The battle of the Busses over the future of their stake in the Los Angeles Lakers is officially becoming a legal matter. Again.

Jeanie Buss has petitioned a Los Angeles Superior Court to block her five siblings from selling the family's remaining 17.8% stake in the Lakers, which she claims to be a scheme to remove her from her role as team governor, according to The Athletic's Sam Amick and Melody Gutierrez .

A court hearing is reportedly scheduled for Nov. 5.

The five other siblings — Johnny, Jim, Janie, Joey and Jesse — announced their intention to sell days after majority owner Mark Walter, who bought the lion's share of the team from the Busses last year, was reported to be selling his stake in the team to Josh Kushner and Bob Iger, at a record valuation of $12.5 billion .

The five siblings reportedly voted to invoke a "tag-along" clause to sell their stake to Kushner and Iger, prompting a response from Jeanie's lawyer declaring any vote to sell as " void ."

Jeanie's 97-page petition reportedly contains five causes of action:

instruct her co-trustees, Joey and Janie, to observe the 2017 court order that requires her co-trustees "to take all actions reasonably available to ensure Jeanie's appointment as Controlling Owner"

declare her siblings' resolution to sell as invalid

not only remove Joey and Janie as co-trustees for "a breach of trust," but also hold them liable "for loss and damage" to the family trust

hold the co-trustees in contempt of court

hold Jim, Johnny and Jesse responsible for "aiding and abetting" Janie and Joey's alleged violation of the 2017 order

In the petition, Jeanie's legal team reportedly argues that selling doesn't make financial sense given the team's "continuously skyrocketing value," which she says will continue under Kushner and Iger.

Under NBA rules, Jeanie also needs a stake of at least 15% in the Lakers to remain the team's governor, a role she was expected to continue occupying for the next four years under Kushner and Iger, a remnant from her deal with Walter. Selling even one sixth of the Buss' remaining stake would take her below that mark.

This could somehow get even uglier for the Buss family

This is only the latest chapter in a breathtakingly cinematic feud among some very rich siblings since the death of patriarch Jerry Buss in 2013.

The first real battle came in 2017, when Jeanie fired Jim from his role as the Lakers' head of basketball operations. That prompted Johnny to challenge her control of the team, which was outlined as part of the trust. The end result was a decisive victory for Jeanie, as a court ruled her co-trustees are obligated to ensure she remains Lakers controlling owner.

It's unclear if that order still applies if the Buss family no longer has a controlling stake at all, as Jeanie is instead fighting for control of the team's remaining minority stake.

Jerry made such infighting nearly inevitable with the "last man standing" provision in his trust, which transfers funds to the remaining siblings when one of the six dies rather than to their own families. Instead of keeping the team together, it has directly incentivized the siblings to sell before their own deaths to pass on their wealth to their children, with Jeanie arguing she has sole control of the keys to any sale.

That tension is now spilling into public view, and it's hard to imagine the other five siblings backing down in court anytime soon.

articles.title: Checking in on the Phillies: What's working and what's not amid their recent hot streak?
articles.summary: Bryce Harper is elite again, and everyone is walking, but something isn't right with Zack Wheeler.
articles.body:
The Phillies arrived in Seattle on a high, with the wind in their sails and a nine-game winning streak at their backs. That run came to an abrupt end on Monday , when the Mariners clobbered Zack Wheeler and limited the Phillies' offense to two runs. After another lackluster offensive showing in a loss Tuesday , the Phillies bounced back Wednesday with a flurry of runs against Bryan Woo .

In all, it was a capable showing. Traveling to Seattle is never easy. Leaving with a victory avoided disaster and sets the Phillies up for a more comfortable series this weekend in Anaheim. All in all, it has been quite the month for this red-pinstriped roller coaster, which went from unwatchable to untouchable in the blink of an eye.

So what's going right? And what's not? Here are four things I'm thinking about the Phillies.

There's something delightfully bizarre about the arrival of Luis Arraez , a player with a microscopic career walk rate, helping to catalyze the Phillies into drawing an avalanche of free passes.

Since the contact maestro's Philadelphia debut on Aug. 4, the club has the single highest walk rate in the sport. Before Arraez showed up, the Phillies ranked 27th. Arraez, for his part, has walked just twice as a Phillie.

It makes sense, then, that his monumental shift in approach traces to before Arraez joined the club. According to The Athletic's Charlotte Varnes , a hitters meeting in late July spurred open conversation about how the entire team could stand to be more selective at the plate. But few souls in that room could've imagined the results being this definitive this quickly. Bryce Harper is walking in more than one-quarter of his plate appearances; Bryson Stott nearly a fifth.

And despite ranking in the bottom-five in runs per game among National League teams for most of the season, the Phillies have led the senior circuit in runs since the beginning of August. It's a remarkable turnaround initiated by a conscious recommitment to discipline.

Much has been made about the inflammatory comments offered by Phillies president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski during last October's end-of-season media conference. Asked about Harper's subpar 2025, Dombrowski didn't pull punches.

"He's still a quality player. He's still an All-Star-caliber player," the longtime exec said. "He didn't have an elite season like he has had in the past. And I guess we only find out if he becomes elite or if he continues to be good."

Harper, as he often does, openly expressed his displeasure with his boss' criticism. At one point over the winter, he was seen taking swings while wearing a T-shirt emblazoned with the words "not elite." Still, he refused to accept Dombrowski's prodding as worthwhile fuel for the fire. He didn't need motivation, he insisted; he's Bryce Harper .

Well, whatever the impetus, Harper has returned to being elite. His .892 OPS ranks seventh in MLB. His .385 OBP ranks sixth. He cranked his 27th homer on Wednesday, matching his tally from 2025. Beyond the lines, Harper has been more engaged and has carried himself with a more upbeat comportment than in years past. Upon Arraez's arrival, he gladly shifted to right field to accommodate a dramatic defensive reshuffle.

Still chasing his first ring, Harper will always be judged by his playoff performance. Coming off his first homerless postseason since 2016, he looks primed to enter this October at his best.

3. The bottom of the lineup looks capable and dangerous

For long stretches throughout the first half, the Phillies' offense was effectively a three-man weave. Harper, Kyle Schwarber and the hirsute Brandon Marsh were tasked with carrying the lineup as Trea Turner , J.T. Realmuto , Alec Bohm and Bryson Stott struggled out of the blocks. Free-agent acquisition Adolis García was a dud and then got hurt. Rookie Justin Crawford looked underbaked and overmatched.

But the baseball season is long and full of opportunity.

Stott has been an .800 OPS hitter for a few months now. Crawford is hitting .300 since May 27. Midseason roster fill-ins Derek Hill and Bryan De La Cruz have both provided a spark. Realmuto has rediscovered competence. Turner authored a stellar July. Arraez brings an entirely new dynamic.

And then there's Bohm, who has gone from Philadelphia's Public Enemy No. 1 to resurrected savior more times than anyone can count. The beginning of this season brought a new low for the curly-haired, lean-limbed infielder, who held a .627 OPS into July. Accordingly, fans were surprised when the complicated defensive realignment following the Arraez trade was done in a way that kept Bohm in the lineup.

Perhaps that was a wake-up call, because Bohm has been fantastic of late, with a near-.900 OPS in August. His resurgence has reshaped the bottom half of this lineup.

There's a lot going well in Philadelphia's starting rotation right now. Cristopher Sánchez continues to sop up innings and WAR on the way to what should be a second straight NL Cy Young runner-up finish. Jesús Luzardo rebounded from a very unlucky start to the year and is rocking a sub-2.50 ERA over his past 21 outings. Aaron Nola has a 2.60 ERA over his past six starts after seeing his season figure exceed 6.00 in late June.

Rookie Andrew Painter , demoted to Triple-A in June, has looked like a different cat since reemerging in late July. His eruption in particular has solidified the back end of a staff that at one point was losing a staggering amount of games started by the fifth spot in the rotation.

Yet this group's most reliable stalwart, Zack Wheeler, that wonderfully gruff, flame-throwing metronome, has slogged through a concerningly substandard stretch. The 36-year-old, who returned from a life-threatening thoracic outlet issue earlier this season, has a 8.51 ERA over his past six starts. After what was shaping up to be the best season of his career , this has been, far and away, the worst stretch of Wheeler's Phillies tenure.

Somewhat reassuringly, Wheeler's issues are mostly command-based and haven't been related to a drop in velocity, always a concern with pitchers on the wrong side of 35. His sinker, the pitch he throws second-most, has been missing arm-side to an outrageous degree. The offering has a zone rate of 34.9% — far, far below Wheeler's career norm. That has led to an uptick in free passes (he walked five the other night in Seattle), something that can doom any pitcher, even one as talented and as experienced as Wheeler. He has also struggled to throw his splitter and breaking balls for strikes. That has forced him to throw his four-seam fastball in the zone more than he'd like, a likely culprit behind this recent schneid.

The long-term concern with Wheeler is mostly moderate. He says he feels strong and healthy coming off the TOS surgery. The stuff isn't backing up. That all points to a hurler who is out of sync, not injured or over-the-hill. Still, with the playoffs rapidly approaching, getting Wheeler right has to be one of this club's top priorities.

articles.title: Trump questions state of MLB while renewing push for Roger Clemens' Hall of Fame induction
articles.summary: Trump listed Roger Clemens' 354 wins and record seven Cy Young Awards on Truth Social, blasting baseball writers for keeping him out of Cooperstown.
articles.body: Major League Baseball is entering the final weeks of its regular season as labor talks between the league and the MLB Players Association reportedly remain stalled, creating uncertainty ahead of the playoffs. The current agreement between the two sides is set to expire on Dec. 1. If they do not reach a new deal by then, a lockout could follow. In July, ESPN reported that the sides’ fundamental disagreement centers on the league’s pursuit of a salary cap system. The union likely prefers to preserve the current system, and neither side appeared willing to move from its position. President Donald Trump has frequently weighed in on sports during his second term. In March, he convened the "Saving College Sports" roundtable, which brought together conference leaders, former coaches and media executives to discuss challenges posed by name, image and likeness deals, the transfer portal and the future of the NCAA. CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM Last month, during MLB All-Star weekend, commissioner Rob Manfred was asked whether he had any sense of whether President Donald Trump might intervene in the league’s labor negotiations. Manfred said at the time he did not want to "speculate" about Trump's potential involvement. "Look, I think it would be wildly, wildly inappropriate for me to speculate what the President of the United States might do or not do in a hypothetical situation," Manfred said. "We know this. He's a great sports fan, and he is really knowledgeable about the business of sports, so it doesn't surprise me." Manfred did say, however, that Trump was "interested." Beyond labor negotiations, Trump has also repeatedly pushed for seven-time Cy Young Award winner Roger Clemens’ induction into the Hall of Fame. In a Truth Social post Wednesday, Trump cited Clemens’ career achievements and criticized Hall of Fame voters over his exclusion. "How about Roger Clemens not being in the National Baseball Hall of Fame and Museum in Cooperstown, New York, all because a bunch of jealous people with far less Talent, voted that he shouldn't be there," Trump wrote. "He was also not convicted, or admitted, to taking Drugs. Roger is easily one of the few Greatest Pitchers of All Time, winning 354 Games, 7 Cy Young Awards (A Record, by 3!), and played in three World Series, winning two! He was third in most Strike-Outs." Trump then turned his attention to Manfred, claiming the commissioner had told him he would approve Pete Rose’s reinstatement but waited until after Rose’s death to do so. "The Commissioner told me he was going to approve Pete Rose, but he waited long enough until Pete died." Last year, Manfred announced that Rose, who died in 2024, and "Shoeless" Joe Jackson would be reinstated, which made both eligible for Hall of Fame consideration. Trump concluded by questioning the state of the sport. "No wonder Baseball is in trouble!" MLB COMMISSIONER UNDERSTANDS WHY TRUMP IS 'INTERESTED' IN MLB CBA NEGOTIATIONS Almost exactly one year ago, on Aug. 24, Trump said he had played golf with Clemens and his son, Kacy. The president then backed Clemens’ Hall of Fame candidacy, writing that the former Boston Red Sox pitcher "should be in the Baseball Hall of Fame, NOW!" Clemens responded on X, writing, "I appreciate the love! DT knows more than anyone the fake news that’s out there. Everyone has their agendas… I played the game to change my family’s direction generationally and to WIN!" CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Clemens’ 10-year run on the Baseball Writers’ Association of America ballot ended in 2022, when he received support from 65.2% of voters, short of the 75% threshold required for election to the Hall of Fame.

Friedl, meanwhile, is in the midst of a disappointing season. After posting a .364 on-base percentage while spending most of his time atop the Reds' lineup last season, he is slashing .158/.242/.234 in 75 games this season. He recently went through an 0-for-30 slump at the plate.

It's been a tough season at the plate for the 31-year-old, but he has still been solid in the outfield, playing both center and left field this year.

Friedl's struggles have cost him his starting spot, as the Reds have turned to J.J. Bleday, Dane Myers and now Hector Rodriguez in the outfield.

With both players having cleared waivers, they'll now remain in Cincinnati.

articles.title: Updated AL East Forecast and Playoff Matchup Predictions For September
articles.summary: It's crunch time in the American League East. As September nears, three teams are still vying for the division title and the other two are in the wild-card hunt.
articles.body:
It's crunch time in the American League East. As September nears, three teams are still vying for the division title and the other two are in the wild-card hunt.

There are so many questions that need answering. What makes each team a real or fake contender? How would the playoff picture look if the season ended today? And in case anyone's curious, what do we think will happen?

Let's break it all down, starting with individual looks at the state of the Tampa Bay Rays, New York Yankees, Boston Red Sox, Baltimore Orioles and Toronto Blue Jays.

Note: Playoff odds are according to FanDuel .

Well, this team has spent a total of 102 days in first place this season. How much more evidence do you need that the Rays are for real?

As per usual, the best explanation of the Rays is a shrug and an "I don't know, they just do everything well." They're above-average offensively (104 OPS+) and pitching-wise (112 ERA+), and they have a case as the AL's best defensive team.

The star power is there, too. Junior Caminero is chasing a second straight 40-homer season. Yandy Díaz leads the AL in hits. Nick Martinez and Drew Rasmussen have sub-3.00 ERAs. Bryan Baker is probably the best closer in the AL. Et cetera.

All good teams have a habit of beating up on less-good teams, but it still stands out that the Rays are a modest 29-23 against winning clubs and 25-20 against their AL East foes. Put them in a fair fight, and they're vulnerable.

The Rays also have "Playoff frauds!" written all over them. The long ball rules in October, and they have gotten just 101 home runs from hitters not named Caminero.

You don't want to face the Yankees' pitching. You just don't. They lead MLB with a 3.23 ERA, and they can be especially dangerous in a short playoff series.

Cam Schlittler, Max Fried and Gerrit Cole? That's a heck of a Game 1-2-3 punch right there. And the more innings they eat, the less relievers not named David Bednar and Brent Headrick will have to do out of the bullpen.

Offensively, the Yankees lead the AL in home runs even without any from Aaron Judge since May. As he's back to taking batting practice, the thinking is that he'll return from his rib injury sometime in September.

Think the Yankees have missed Judge? Since he last played on May 31, they are only five games over .500 and have outscored just two other teams.

As such, it isn't a reach to think that the Yankees' path to the World Series is contingent on Judge being Judge again. That's a lot to ask of a guy who has missed basically three months, and who doesn't have time for a long ramp-up.

The Red Sox have won 41 out of their last 55 games. The last time they did that was in 2018, when they went on to win the World Series.

They're the only team in the AL with as many as four 3-WAR hitters. Their bullpen sports an MLB-best 2.85 ERA. They have four starters who can give them a quality start any given time out.

Boston also stands to get as big of a health boost as any team in MLB in September. Roman Anthony, Trevor Story and Curtis Mead should return. So could Garrett Crochet, whose past experience as a reliever could make him extremely useful even if starting again in 2026 is highly unlikely.

The Red Sox have survived Crochet's absence during the regular season, but can they keep that up if they make the playoffs? Without him, they have no true No. 1 starter. That doesn't tend to be an advantage come October.

There's also something fishy about the "Different guy every night!" thing Boston has benefited from during its surge. Are guys like Nick Sogard and Mickey Gasper really difference-makers? Or are they merely randos having a moment in the sun?

If you gave up on the Orioles when they fell to a season-low nine games under .500 on July 8, just know that they are 23-17 ever since.

It's mostly because they have remembered how to pitch, to the tune of a 3.63 ERA. Trevor Rogers, Shane Baz and Kyle Bradish have led the way, with each making at least seven starts and pitching to an ERA in the 3.00s.

Otherwise, Pete Alonso has determined that now is his time to shine. He's ripped off a 1.040 OPS and 11 home runs since the All-Star break, and the latter count is notably one less than it should be .

As hot as Alonso is, this offense's OPS has actually gone down from the first half to the second. It's a .227/.310/.390 slash line, which is just not good.

That's the ballgame right there, and it's not like Alonso has much hope of getting any weight off his shoulders. Adley Rutschman and Taylor Ward are gone, and "Missing" posters remain up for the 2022-25 version of Gunnar Henderson.

The Blue Jays were 10 games under .500 as of July 28, prompting the front office to sell off assets like Kevin Gausman, Jeff Hoffman and Daulton Varsho at the trade deadline.

They have since gone 16-10, in part aided by some fantastic pitching from Dylan Cease. He's allowed a total of 10 earned runs in his last nine starts, with 81 strikeouts over 61.0 innings pitched.

Toronto is otherwise still waiting on its offense to wake up. Who knows? Just as Cal Raleigh has finally found his stroke in Seattle, perhaps Vladimir Guerrero Jr. can do the same and put the Blue Jays lineup on his shoulders.

Did that come off as a blatant attempt to competence-wash this offense? Because that's what it was. They're the lowest-scoring team in MLB, and Guerrero's funk somehow seems worse than Raleigh's. Guerrero isn't batting in the .100s, but at least Raleigh can go deep in his home park.

Also, Cease is one of few Toronto pitchers who isn't hurt. Shane Bieber just landed on the injured list , making it an even 10 hurlers on the IL for Toronto.

As the No. 1 seed in the American League playoff field, the Rays would get a first-round bye and then host the winner of the No. 5 vs. No. 4 seeds in the Wild Card Series in the Division Series at Tropicana Field.

As of now, it looks like they would face an AL East rival one way or another. Both the AL West and the AL's third wild card are basically races to .500, and the Red Sox (13 games) and Yankees (18 games) are safely above that threshold.

These two long-standing rivals are on track to meet in the Wild Card Series for a best of three at Yankee Stadium.

Either could still win the AL East and grab a first-round bye. Failing that, the only question is whether Boston can pull ahead and ensure that they would host the Yankees at Fenway Park. The Red Sox have won 22 of their last 29 home games.

They're out of the money for now, but Orioles (2.5 GB) and Blue Jays (3.0 GB) are within shouting distance of the Guardians in the wild card race.

According to FanGraphs , Baltimore's and Toronto's chances of making the postseason sit at 13.1 and 10.2 percent, respectively.

Hard: 3 @ ATL, 4 @ NYY, 3 @ PHI, 4 @ TEX, 3 vs. BOS, 3 vs. SDP, 3 vs. HOU

This is a pretty brutal remaining schedule for the Rays, especially with a good chunk of their "hard" series set to be on the road. They're 43-23 at Tropicana Field, compared to 36-31 away from home.

Hard: 3 @ SDP, 3 @ ARI, 4 vs. TBR, 4 vs. BOS

Soft: 3 vs. COL, 3 vs. NYM, 3 vs. BAL, 3 @ LAA, 3 @ MIN

The Yankees have losing records against the Rays (3-6) and Red Sox (4-5), so those upcoming matchups loom large. Still, any damage they incur in those series could be offset if they stomp the lightweights in their path.

Hard: 3 @ TBR, 4 @ NYY, 3 @ TEX, 3 vs. CHC, 3 vs. CLE

Soft: 3 vs. LAA, 3 vs. KCR, 3 vs. SEA, 4 @ BAL

The Red Sox are only looking up at six teams in the MLB standings, and they still have to play three of them. That's rough, and even the "soft" portion of their remaining schedule needs some asterisks. The Orioles and Seattle Mariners are playoff contenders, after all.

Hard: 3 @ NYY, 3 vs. MIL, 4 vs. BOS, 3 vs. CLE

Soft: 3 vs. TOR, 3 @ TOR, 3 @ COL, 3 @ ATH, 3 @ NYM

On that last point, six remaining games against the Blue Jays arguably shouldn't count as "soft" for the Orioles. They'll also need to bring their A game against the four proper contenders coming up. Baltimore is 33-36 against winning clubs.

Soft: 3 vs. DET, 3 vs. CIN, 3 vs. SEA, 3 vs. BAL, 3 @ BAL, 3 @ KCR, 3 @ ATH

If the Blue Jays are going to make a move in the final month of the regular season, it's clear how it's going to happen. This is about as soft as remaining schedules get, and it's a chance for them to improve on a 29-24 performance against teams with losing records.

This might be a case of recency bias run amok, but whatever. The Red Sox have shaved 9.5 games off their AL East deficit just since June 25. What's another 6.0 games by September 27?

It can happen if they keep it up and the Rays backslide even a little. The latter is already underway, as Tampa Bay is limping toward its hard finish to the year with losses in eight out of 13.

AL East Wild Cards: New York Yankees and Tampa Bay Rays

This is meant to be in order, meaning the Yankees would take the No. 4 seed and the Rays would take the No. 5 seed.

It would represent a stunning fall for the Rays, but their recent skid ahead of a hard schedule feels like a recipe for the inevitable. They have statistically been baseball's luckiest team , and are thus its most prone to regression.

For their part, the Yankees' pitching is firmly within the circle of trust at this point. Their arms can carry them even if Judge needs time to go full-Judge, though one wonders if his return alone could have a galvanizing effect on the offense.

AL Wild Card Series: Tampa Bay Rays (5) at New York Yankees (4)

AL Wild Card Series: Cleveland Guardians (6) at Seattle Mariners (3)

First-Round Byes: Chicago White Sox (2), Boston Red Sox (1)

Stats courtesy of Baseball Reference , FanGraphs and Baseball Savant .

We're one step closer to the bracket finals of the 2026 Little League World Series (LLWS). Wednesday's slate brought four exciting matchups that have set the stage for the lower-bracket finals.

International Champion vs. USA Champion at 3 p.m. ET on ABC

Curaçao Makes a Statement, Weather Prompts Change in Thursday Schedule

Wednesday's action started with a bang, as the representative from Curaçao, Pariba Little League, jumped out to a massive early lead over Ministerio Sobre Las Alas Del Águila Little League (Latin America).

Curaçao made a statement with a 10-run second inning that had Latin America on the proverbial ropes for the rest of the game. Latin America answered with three runs in the fourth, but it wasn't nearly enough.

Pariba Little League added a pair of insurance runs in the sixth to close out a nine-run victory. It's another big step for Pariba Little League, which defeated its Williamstead rival Pabao Little League in a seven-game series to represent the Curaçao region.

This is also the first tournament to feature a Curaçao region. Pabao Little League was the LLWS runner-up in both 2022 and 2023 as representatives of the Caribbean Region.

Paseo Verde Little League (Mountain) and West Side Little League (Great Lakes) also won convincingly on Wednesday, but as the first official representative of the Curaçao region, Pariba is making history.

Curaçao moves on to the international final, while Latin America will play in one of Thursday morning's two contests. The games have been moved to the morning due to incoming inclement weather.

Latin America and Japan will play in the international lower-bracket semifinal at Volunteer Stadium on Thursday, while the Great Lakes and Midwest teams will face off at Howard J. Lamade Stadium.

articles.title: 10 MLB September Call-Ups Ready to Make Major Impact on Playoff Races
articles.summary: The final month of the 2026 MLB regular season is fast approaching, and the calendar flipping to September also means that active rosters expand from 26 to 28 players across baseball.
articles.body:
The final month of the 2026 MLB regular season is fast approaching, and the calendar flipping to September also means that active rosters expand from 26 to 28 players across baseball.

The days of roster swelling to as many as 40 players ended in 2021, and with the more streamlined rules, those two additional spots carry added significance for contenders looking to bolster the roster for the playoff push.

To that point, Trey Yesavage (TOR) and Connelly Early (BOS) both ended up starting playoff games last October after debuting as September call-ups.

We've highlighted 10 players who could be the headliners of this year's September roster additions, with each one offering a legitimate chance to make an impact for a contending club.

Stats: 99 G, .314/.397/.564, 47 XBH (23 HR), 6 SB

Why He's Ready: Already widely regarded as the best defensive infielder in the Red Sox system, Franklin Arias has taken his offensive game to new heights this season. His slugging percentage has climbed a staggering 176 points despite making the jump to the upper levels of the minors, and he has done it while also improving his walk rate from 7.2 to 10.7 percent.

Projected Role: With Trevor Story sidelined, the Red Sox have leaned on Andruw Monasterio as their primary shortstop for the past month. Story is on the rehab trail, but he had a 54 OPS+ in 176 plate appearances before undergoing sports hernia surgery, and he's 4-for-25 with seven strikeouts at Triple-A.

Meanwhile, Arias is batting .301/.368/.495 with 10 extra-base hits in 24 games since he was promoted to Triple-A. He has started seeing reps at second base, so there is a potential secondary path if the starting shortstop job is indeed still waiting for Story.

Stats: 80 G, .332/.433/.524, 29 XBH (13 HR), 19 SB

Why He's Ready: The No. 43 overall pick in the 2025 draft, Cam Cannarella is already knocking on the MLB door thanks to his 55-hit, 60-speed toolbox. After crushing High-A and Double-A pitching to open the year, he has a .273/.405/.384 line over 27 games since he was promoted to Triple-A while logging a healthy 15.7 percent walk rate.

Projected Role: The Marlins are 25th in the majors in runs scored (139) since the All-Star break, and they could use a spark while they pursue a wild-card berth. A year ago, Jakob Marsee provided just that when he joined the team on Aug. 1, and Cannarella could provide a similar jolt.

With Owen Caissie (51 PA, .178/.275/.289, 31.4 K%) and Esteury Ruiz (50 PA, .200/.360/.300, 36.0 K%) both struggling in August, there is a clear path for him to play his way into a regular role down the stretch.

Stats: 107 G, .293/.376/.466, 43 XBH (10 HR), 58 SB

Why He's Ready: Patrick Clohisy was the No. 29 prospect in a relatively thin Atlanta farm system to start the year, according to Baseball America . A .284/.390/.383 line over 21 games in the 2025 Arizona Fall League helped elevate his prospect stock, and that has carried over to a breakout 2026 campaign. In 37 games since moving up to Triple-A, he is hitting .357/.440/.512 with 13 extra-base hits and 21 steals.

Projected Role: With speed and the ability to play all three outfield spots, Clohisy is the type of player who can slot seamlessly onto the big league bench and provide value without seeing regular playing time.

That said, his stellar performance at Triple-A along with the lackluster production from Mike Yastrzemski and Lane Thomas in a left field platoon cracks the door for him to potentially seize a bigger role.

Stats: 15 G, 14 GS, 3.13 ERA, 1.13 WHIP, 29 BB, 79 K, 77.2 IP

Why He's Ready: The Brewers acquired right-hander Coleman Crow in the deal that sent Adrian Houser and Tyrone Taylor to the Mets prior to the 2024 season, and he made his MLB debut in April.

He didn't find immediate success in the big leagues, but continued to thrive back at Triple-A, and with 18.2 scoreless innings over his last three starts he has earned another look.

Projected Role: While he made four spot starts earlier this season, Crow would slot into a multi-inning role in the Milwaukee bullpen down the stretch where his high-spin curveball could be a major weapon.

The Brewers figure to lean heavily on mixing and matching arms in October behind ace Jacob Misiorowski, and Crow is capable of pitching his way onto the playoff roster with a strong September showing.

Stats: 18 G, 10 GS, 2.90 ERA, 0.97 WHIP, 22 BB, 80 K, 59.0 IP

Why He's Ready: The Rays acquired Ty Johnson from the Cubs in the Isaac Paredes deal at the 2024 trade deadline, and over the past two seasons he has carried a 34.6 percent strikeout rate in the upper levels of the minors. He was moved to the bullpen at the end of July in advance of a potential call-up, and he has a .161 opponents' batting average and 14.0 K/9 in 9.2 innings as a reliever.

Projected Role: Despite a more traditional starting staff than usual with Drew Rasmussen, Shane McClanahan, Nick Martinez and deadline pickup Freddy Peralta all capable of pitching deep into games, Tampa Bay has always done an excellent job fully utilizing its bullpen.

With a dynamic fastball-slider combination, Johnson has the stuff to make an immediate splash in shorter stints, with his wipeout slider a legitimate putaway pitch that could earn him some high-leverage opportunities.

Stats: 20 G, 17 GS, 2.92 ERA, 1.13 WHIP, 38 BB, 112 K, 83.1 IP

Why He's Ready: Arguably the top pitching prospect in a thin Houston system, Bryce Mayer has come a long way in a short time since going in the 14th round of the 2024 draft. After a shaky Triple-A debut on Aug. 8, he has allowed six hits and one earned run over 11.1 innings in his two most recent outings, and he increasingly looks like a finished product.

Projected Role: The Astros have often eased their young starters into the big leagues in a relief role, and with a mid-90s fastball and two solid breaking balls, he has a repertoire that could potentially play up in shorter stints.

Then again, considering how Cristian Javier (4 GS, 5.68 ERA, 19.0 IP), Peter Lambert (4 GS, 6.98 ERA, 19.1 IP) and Ethan Pecko (2 GS, 7.88 ERA, 8.0 IP) have pitched in August, a shot at the rotation is also not out of the question.

Stats: 119 G, .300/.423/.559, 57 XBH (27 HR), 7 SB

Why He's Ready: The Dodgers have a wealth of exciting young outfield talent, but none is more MLB-ready than James Tibbs III, who has spent the entire 2026 season crushing Triple-A pitching. With a .360/.490/.640 line over 98 plate appearances in August, he is swinging it well enough to warrant a call-up.

Projected Role: Tibbs has yet to reach the majors largely because of the Dodgers' crowded outfield., but that changed when Andy Pages suffered a fractured hand on Aug. 21.

Tibbs is strictly a corner outfielder, so he's not a direct replacement, and Alek Thomas earned the initial call-up to fill the gap in center field. That said, there is always room for another productive bat on the roster. Tibbs could serve as a pinch-hit option for Thomas late in games, with Tommy Edman shifting from second base to center field.

1B/OF Ralphy Velazquez, Cleveland Guardians

Stats: 106 G, .293/.379/.561, 52 XBH (27 HR), 2 SB

Why He's Ready: Over 18 games at the Triple-A level in August, Ralphy Velazquez is hitting .371/.438/.986 with 14 home runs and 27 RBI. What more really needs to be said about his MLB readiness?

Projected Role: Considering the Guardians rank 28th in the majors with 18 home runs in 22 games this month, they should be rolling out the red carpet for Velazquez to fill whatever role best suits him.

The 21-year-old fits best at first base, where he would be an immediate upgrade over deadline pickup Nathaniel Lowe, who has an 83 OPS+ in 17 games since joining the Guardians. He has also started 20 games in left field in the minors this year and would pencil nicely into the DH role as well.

One way or another, he's one of the best nine bats in the organization right now.

Stats: 15 G, 11 GS, 6.88 ERA, 1.76 WHIP, 30 BB, 44 K, 35.1 IP

Why He's Ready: A consensus Top 100 prospect entering the 2026 season, Jaxon Wiggins has struggled through a trying season that was derailed early by elbow inflammation. His 6.88 ERA and 18.3 percent walk rate don't scream immediate impact, but he was moved to the bullpen on Aug. 11 and has struck out seven of the 16 batters he's faced over four no-hit frames.

Projected Role: With a 60-grade fastball that tops out at 101 mph and a wipeout slider, it's easy to envision Wiggins pitching his way onto the playoff roster based on pure arm talent.

His spotty command makes it unlikely he will see high-leverage work, at least initially, but his swing-and-miss stuff and ability to go multiple innings have plenty of value to a Cubs team in need of additional arms.

Stats: 22 GS, 4.11 ERA, 1.21 WHIP, 27 BB, 117 K, 81.0 IP

Why He's Ready: Just a year removed from going No. 26 overall in the 2025 draft, Gage Wood has firmly established himself as one of baseball's top pitching prospects. He is currently pitching at Double-A, but young pitchers skipping over the Triple-A level is not uncommon, especially for a late-season debut.

Projected Role: With rookie Andrew Painter coming off seven innings of five-hit, one-run ball in his last start, any thoughts of Wood stealing the No. 5 starter job down the stretch are likely misplaced.

However, he spent his first two seasons at the University of Arkansas pitching almost exclusively out of the bullpen, and that's where he could make a bigger impact for the Phillies. In 2023, Orion Kerkering made the playoff roster after just three regular-season appearances and ended up finding his way into seven games in the playoffs, so there is some precedent.

articles.title: Pete Crow-Armstrong Calls Out Umpires for 'Pretty Obvious' Missed Call in Cubs' Loss to D-Backs
articles.summary: The already chippy series between the Chicago Cubs and Arizona Diamondbacks added another layer on Wednesday night, only this time it was the umpires on the receiving end of Pete Crow-Armstrong's ire.
articles.body:
The already chippy series between the Chicago Cubs and Arizona Diamondbacks added another layer on Wednesday night, only this time it was the umpires on the receiving end of Pete Crow-Armstrong's ire.

Speaking to reporters after the Cubs' 2-0 loss, Crow-Armstrong called out the umps for a "pretty obvious" missed call on an apparent balk by D-Backs starter Eduardo Rodriguez in the top of the sixth.

"I saw four umpires miss a pretty obvious play," he said. "They're out there every day, just like we are. Their one job is to get calls right, and if they get it wrong, they're supposed to talk about it, figure it out and get it right. And they didn't."

MLB September Call-Ups Ready to Make Impact

The missed call occurred when Crow-Armstrong was on third base with two outs when he was getting a secondary lead off the bag. Rodriguez went into his wind up when his back leg came off the mound like he was trying to step off after catcher James McCann come out of his crouch for a pitch-out as he delivered the ball to the plate.

Crew chief Alfonso Márquez acknowledged after the game when the umps were able to review the footage that a balk should have been called.

"We just didn't see it," he said. "After looking at the video, it looked like [Rodriguez] stepped off."

Since the play isn't reviewable, the Cubs were unable to call for a challenge. The umps convened to discuss the play before deciding a balk did not occur.

Michael Busch walked later in the at-bat, but the inning ended when Rodriguez struck out Nico Hoerner to keep the scoreless tie intact.

If the balk had been called, Crow-Armstrong would have scored to put the Cubs ahead 1-0.

Arizona would take the lead in the bottom of the sixth on Jordan Lawlar's homer off Matthew Boyd to leadoff the frame. The Diamondbacks added a second run in the bottom of the eighth on Ryan Waldschmidt's sacrifice fly.

It's entirely possible the Cubs would have lost even if Crow-Armstrong had been awarded home, but a tie game in the later innings could have changed the pitching strategy for manager Craig Counsell.

Crow-Armstrong's outburst at the umps came two days after Diamondbacks pitcher Merrill Kelly lashed out at the Cubs when he accused third base coach Quintin Berry of stealing signs during Monday's 7-0 win for Chicago.

D-Backs manager Torey Lovullo formally apologized to the Cubs for the sign-stealing situation prior to Tuesday's game after receiving an explanation from MLB senior vice president of on-field operations Michael Hill.

Arizona took two out of three games in the series between NL wild card contenders. The Cubs (76-58) own the top wild card spot, though they have struggled recently with five losses in their last seven games.

The Diamondbacks (71-63) trail the San Diego Padres by one game for the third and final wild card spot in the NL. The NL West rivals play a three-game series in San Diego from Sept. 25-27 to close out the regular season.

articles.title: Little League World Series 2026 Final Scores, Bracket Results, Thursday Highlights
articles.summary: Even with impending weather forcing the Little League World Series to adjust Thursday's schedule, the U.S. and international finals are now set.
articles.body:
Even with impending weather forcing the Little League World Series to adjust Thursday's schedule, the U.S. and international finals are now set.

Ohio defeated Iowa in the game at Lamade Stadium to reach the United States championship where it will take on Nevada.

The international semifinal saw Japan defeat Nicaragua to reach the final against Curaçao.

For the first time since 2021 and just the second time in the state's history, Ohio will play for the U.S. championship after a 7-1 victory over Iowa.

The team from Hamilton West Side rode a four-run first inning to victory. Bob Frazier had the big hit with a three-run triple after Jack McAdams opened the scoring with an RBI single.

Walker Osborne was staked to a 4-0 lead before throwing his first pitch. He remained calm throughout his start, throwing a complete game with four strikeouts and one run allowed over six innings.

Next up for Ohio will be a showdown with Nevada in a rematch of their Aug. 21 game. Nevada won that contest 6-5 in what has been its one close call in the tournament thus far. The Henderson squad has outscored Washington and Iowa 19-6 in its last two games.

Ohio responded to the loss with five consecutive wins and has outscored opponents 39-6 during this stretch.

Japan rode a combination of stellar pitching from Shinnosuke Ijima and timely hitting in the fifth inning to defeat Nicaragua 4-1 in the international semifinal.

Ijima was terrific on the mound with 11 strikeouts in a complete game victory. He allowed one run on four hits and threw 87 pitches.

The pitching on both sides was strong to start the game. After three scoreless innings, Nicaragua finally broke through in the top of the fourth thanks to José Martínez's RBI single to make it a 1-0 game.

Ijima, in addition to his dominance on the mound, helped himself at the plate in the bottom of the frame with an RBI single that tied the score.

Rui Tobata and Tensei Yazawa broke the stalemate in the fifth with back-to-back RBI doubles to put Japan ahead 4-1. Ijima closed out the game by striking out all three hitters he faced in the sixth.

This marks Japan's first appearance in the international championship game since 2019. It will go up against a Curaçao team that has outscored its three opponents 18-3 thus far, including a 6-0 victory over Japan on Aug. 21.

articles.title: MLB Reportedly Proposes 'Drastic Changes' to Offseason Schedule, Free-Agency in New CBA Proposal
articles.summary: Major League Baseball is proposing a dramatic change to the league's offseason schedule regarding when teams can and can't sign free agents, per ESPN's Jeff Passan, who broke it down:
articles.body:
Major League Baseball is proposing a dramatic change to the league's offseason schedule regarding when teams can and can't sign free agents, per ESPN's Jeff Passan , who broke it down:

"A free agent dead period until the first day of the Winter Meetings in early December in which players and teams can negotiate but no deals can be signed. Trades would be allowed during this period."

"Free agency would open the Monday the Winter Meetings begin and would close Dec. 21."

"From Dec. 21 through the first Monday in February, no free agent signings or trades would be allowed."

"Free agents could sign and trades would be allowed again from the first Monday in February onward."

Bob Nightengale of USA Today provided more information.

Speaking of an apparent player union rejection, MLBPA interim executive director Bruce Meyer had this to say on the matter, per Passan. In short, it's clear the players' union isn't in favor here.

"The league, through their propaganda arm, is promoting their latest set of roster and transaction proposals as player-friendly.

"MLB expressly conditioned these proposals on the players' agreement to a salary cap system, which would drastically reduce overall player compensation, eliminate fully guaranteed contracts through escrow, and turn back the clock on fundamental player rights.

"Their latest proposals regarding free agency would eliminate Player rights by establishing an artificial free agency window, subject to a salary cap, which would reduce player leverage and create a game of musical chairs pitting player vs. player.

"The suggestion that the only way to limit roster churn, or incentivize earlier Free Agent signings is with a salary cap is entirely unserious. Players have proposed changes that would address these priorities, but the league is not interested in any changes that don't directly reduce the rights of all players and shift leverage to the owners."
