articles.title: Sal Stewart vs JJ Wetherholt for top NL rookie not close | Chris Young
articles.summary: MLB Network's Chris Young had a strong take about NL Rookie of the Year candidates Sal Stewart and JJ Wetherholt, one with which many Reds fans agree.
articles.body:
MLB Network's Chris Young had a strong take on " MLB Central " about top National League Rookie of the Year candidates Sal Stewart and JJ Wetherholt , and it's one with which many Cincinnati Reds fans will agree.

"With the team aspect, I really don't bring that into account," Young said. "Rookie of the Year is a straight numbers award. It's always been. And it's an offensive award. … And I want to make sure to come off clear: This by no means is a knock on what JJ has done this year. JJ has had an amazing rookie season. But this should not be a close race. You're talking about 28 (homers) and 100 (RBIs) right now.

"It leads me to believe, that WAR − even though it's not a scam, it's getting a little scam-ish. Sorry, when you look at the numbers side-by-side: If I'm Sal, I'm expecting to win this award. (With WAR), you're telling me that JJ Wetherholt is twice the player of Sal Stewart? That is hard for me to believe. Maybe WAR needs to be recalibrated to an extent, especially when it comes to first basemen."

He played for the Reds!? Do you remember these players' time in Cincy?

Wetherholt's WAR is 4.8; Stewart's is 1.9.

Mark DeRosa added during the broadcast that NL Rookie of the Year is "going to be a dogfight," but he's leaning toward Stewart deserving the award.

articles.title: MLB Proposes Weeks-Long Free Agent Signing Window, Lowering In-Season Options
articles.summary: Major League Baseball has proposed limiting free-agent signings to several weeks in December, among other items.
articles.body: Major League Baseball has proposed limiting free-agent signings to several weeks in December and then from early February in each offseason, along with a ban on trades during the gap in between. The plan aims to create more of an offseason transaction flurry similar to those in the NFL and NBA. The plan offered to the players' association Thursday is contingent on adoption of the salary cap system MLB proposed in May, which the union has vowed never to accept. MLB also proposed lowering the maximum in-season options to the minor leagues from five to four and adopting a system of weekly rosters. Teams would be allowed 14 pitchers, up from 13, when the 26-man roster limit is in effect from the season’s start through Aug. 31. The union did not immediately respond publicly to the new proposal. Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: Aaron Judge Reveals Yankees Return Plans amid Rib Injury Rehab During MLB Playoff Race
articles.summary: Aaron Judge hasn't played since May 31 because of a fractured right rib, but he doesn't plan on making any rehab appearances when he is ready to return despite all that time off.
articles.body:
Aaron Judge hasn't played since May 31 because of a fractured right rib, but he doesn't plan on making any rehab appearances when he is ready to return despite all that time off.

"Why waste at-bats?" he told reporters Thursday. "Why waste anything down in a minor-league game? I've been doing this for a while now, and I've got a sense of what I need to do on the field and how to manage it."

Judge also said "there haven't been any setbacks, which has been the greatest thing," while pointing out he didn't make a minor league rehab appearance in 2023 either even though he missed nearly two months due to a toe injury.

What's more, he said he plans on being the right fielder and not a designated hitter, adding he will "play smart" in regards to diving.

"I feel like if I tell them I'm ready to go play, I think we're ready to go play," Judge said. "I'm not a pitcher. I'm a position player. I get my reps down here in the cage, and I've been to every game. I've been sitting there in the dugout watching every game."

It should be noted Yankees manager Aaron Boone told reporters "we'll make that decision collectively" when discussing whether the team will ask Judge to make a rehab appearance.

Still, no rehab appearances would mean getting him into the lineup quicker. And that is exactly what the Yankees need to do considering some of their offensive struggles without his bat in the middle of the order.

Brendan Kuty and Chris Kirschner of The Athletic noted they are 26th in the league in runs scored and 29th in wRC+ since their first game without Judge on June 2.

It is a credit to the pitching that New York is still 75-57 overall and in the top wild-card spot in the American League. It is also still just 3.5 games behind the Tampa Bay Rays in the AL East and could make a late push for the division if and when the slugger returns.

When healthy, Judge is one of the best players in the sport. His resume includes three AL MVPs, an AL Rookie of the Year, a batting title, eight All-Star selections and five Silver Sluggers.

He was well on his way to adding to those totals this season before the setback and was slashing .248/.375/.533 with 17 home runs and 38 RBI in 59 games.

While the Yankees have done an excellent job of remaining in the playoff picture without him, they likely need Judge back if they are going to deliver on World Series expectations. He sounded like someone who is preparing for a return on Thursday, even if that return will not include a rehab appearance.

articles.title: Tarik Skubal Expects 'Emotional' Return in 1st Game vs. Tigers Since Dodgers Trade
articles.summary: For the first time since being traded, Tarik Skubal will go up against his former team as the Los Angeles Dodgers host the Detroit Tigers this weekend.
articles.body:
For the first time since being traded, Tarik Skubal will go up against his former team as the Los Angeles Dodgers host the Detroit Tigers this weekend.

Skubal said the matchup "will be emotional there just because of the history."

"We'll see, right?" Skubal told SI.com on Wednesday (h/t Charles Odum of the Associated Press). "The whole process was emotional. I have a lot of respect for those guys over there. I'm just going to go play baseball."

His future with the Tigers was in limbo for much of the last two years as he and Detroit continued to be far apart on a contract, so the trade didn't come as all that much of a surprise.

"But at the end of the day, I've got to go play baseball," Skubal said. "I've got to compete and do what I do well, what makes me a good pitcher. I'll probably handle the emotions after."

articles.title: Kirk Cousins has another solid outing for Raiders, while Fernando Mendoza struggles
articles.summary: Raiders tight end Brock Bowers saw his first snaps of the preseason.
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders decided months ago that they preferred Kirk Cousins starting the season at quarterback while Fernando Mendoza sat and learned.

Based on preseason results, it seems like that might be a reasonable call.

Cousins played in two of the Raiders' preseason games and generally looked sharp and confident in new coach Klint Kubiak's offense. He played two possessions on Thursday night against the San Francisco 49ers, and the Raiders got a field goal on each of them. Mendoza, the first pick of this year's NFL Draft, had some good preseason moments, too, but he threw an interception for the second straight game and generally struggled.

Mendoza's second pass of the game was a pick. Mendoza tried to squeeze a pass over the 49ers' linebackers dropping into coverage and it was high to Jalen Nailor. The pass went off Nailor's hands and was picked off. That was Mendoza's second interception of the preseason. The first was a pick-6 in last week's game against the Texans.

Mendoza was sacked twice and had just 38 passing yards in the first half. He had four drives before halftime: two ended with a punt, one with an interception and then the Raiders got a field goal before halftime.

The Raiders should be pleased with what they saw out of their starting offense, and also the potential of Mendoza. They also had some teaching moments for the rookie in the preseason.

The Raiders used the starting offense in their first preseason game, and didn't use any starters in the second game. But the first game didn't include tight end Brock Bowers. Bowers was targeted on Cousins' first two passes, which is probably a sign of things to come this season. Rookie running back Mike Washington Jr. got the start instead of injured Ashton Jeanty. He got five carries for 20 yards on the first series. He got three more carries for 29 yards on the second drive. Washington looked good, though it was risky to give any back that many carries with Jeanty's status for the opener uncertain.

As he did in the first preseason game, Cousins was sharp on the first drive. He spread the ball around and looked comfortable in the offense. Cousins hit 4-of-5 passes for 45 yards and the Raiders got a field goal. Cousins stayed in for another series after that, and led another field goal drive.

Cousins was done after two drives. He was 8 of 11 for just 51 yards but the offense was productive. He played three possessions in the preseason and the Raiders scored points on all three of them. He wasn't great but it was a reasonable outing, and certainly didn't give the Raiders a second thought on their plan to start him in Week 1.

A year after the Raiders struggled to do anything right, the offense looks like it could be much more competitive.

Mendoza came in after Cousins and immediately got hit. He rolled to his left, turned his hips and got a pass out just as he got hit. Nailor made a nice one-handed catch. Then came the interception, which was a forced pass that was an unnecessary risk.

The second series didn't go anywhere as Mendoza threw incomplete on second down and was sacked on third down. The Raiders went three-and-out and punted.

Mendoza did get a field-goal drive going at the end of the half, and the biggest play was a defensive pass interference that gained 26 yards. Mendoza went 5 of 9 for just 38 yards in the first half. His passer rating was 26.4. It was a stark contrast to Mendoza's preseason debut, when he looked comfortable and made plays.

Mendoza played into the third quarter. His first pass should have been a short, easy completion but he threw it too high and it went off his intended receiver's hands. He calmed down after that and drove the team into field-goal range, though the field goal missed. Mendoza was done after that, as Aidan O'Connell took over late in the third quarter. Mendoza's final line was 7 of 14 for 57 yards.

Mendoza should be fine over time. But the Raiders had a plan to let him sit and wait for a while. Mendoza provided some reasons why over the preseason.

articles.summary: It was a pitchers' duel between Chris Sale and Yoshinobu Yamamoto. The Braves ace won.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Braves ace threw a shutout against the Los Angeles Dodgers on Thursday, finishing off a three-game sweep with a 1-0 win. The game was billed as a pitchers' duel against Dodgers ace Yoshinobu Yamamoto and he most certainly delivered.

Sale's final line: 9 innings, 5 hits, 0 runs, 0 walks and 11 strikeouts (tying a season high) on 109 pitches. He finished things off with a punchout of Alex Call.

The 37-year-old Sale turned back the clock in multiple ways. It was his first shutout since 2019, a span of time that includes 117 starts, three All-Star selections and the 2024 NL Cy Young Award. Only five older pitchers have thrown a shutout with double-digit strikeouts and no walks in MLB's modern era : Cy Young, Eddie Plank, Steve Carlton, Nolan Ryan and Randy Johnson.

He also found some rare heat against the Dodgers' most dangerous hitter. Facing Shohei Ohtani in the third inning, Sale threw a 100.1 mph fastball, his fastest pitch since July 6, 2018 according to MLB.com's Sarah Langs .

Sale later struck out Ohtani on a 99.6 mph pitch, his second-hardest offering of the night. He didn't hide the extra effort while speaking with reporters after the game, per 680 The Fan's Will Hopkins :

"He's probably the best I've ever seen. And when you're facing the best, you got to bring your best."

On the Dodgers' side, Yamamoto had a perfectly fine outing with 6 1/3 innings, 4 hits, 1 run, 1 walk and 8 strikeouts. His only run, the lone run of the game, came on his first pitch when Braves catcher Drake Baldwin got a hold of a hanging splitter for a 402-foot homer.

Yamamoto and the Dodgers' bullpen allowed only three more hits the entire game, all singles, but their offense couldn't muster the needed run against Sale.

It was a meaningful performance for Sale, who revealed he was playing with a heavy heart and perhaps some help, via Hopkins :

"We lost a close family friend tonight. Her name was Ashley Foss. She was 42 years old. Just tough. She was battling for the longest time. I was texting with her family today. It's tough. She was a huge Braves fan. She watched all these games. It felt weird out there because it felt like I had a little something else helping me tonight. There's no question that was her out there."

The Braves' win is significant as far as MLB playoff seeding goes. Atlanta is now only one game back from the Dodgers for the No. 2 seed in the NL, with the Milwaukee Brewers sitting just ahead at an MLB-best 82-51.

More concerning for the Dodgers is that they are now 1-12 since July 31 against teams currently holding a playoff spot. With the postseason just over a month away, that's not exactly the best sign for the two-time defending champions.

articles.title: They were among baseball’s best teams last year. Now they could miss the playoffs.
articles.summary: The Seattle Mariners and the Tampa Bay Rays were World Series contenders last season but are struggling mightily just to reach the postseason.
articles.body: The Toronto Blue Jays were two outs away from winning the World Series last season. Nine months later, they might not even make the playoffs. “We got to start winning,” Blue Jays manager John Schneider said in July as his team fell under .500. “That’s just the bottom line.” That regression would seem to have opened an opportunity for the Seattle Mariners, who lost to Toronto in last year’s American League Championship Series ... if the Mariners weren’t similarly having trouble following up their own breakthrough 2025 season. “Ultimately, we’re just playing very, very, very bad baseball in every facet of the game,” Mariners star Cal Raleigh told reporters this month. That isn’t how either franchise envisioned this season going when they began the spring with enormous expectations and anticipation for how both might follow up each team’s best season in a generation. Last season, the Jays’ 94 wins tied for the American League’s best record with the New York Yankees, while Seattle had 90 wins. Now, as the teams meet Friday for a three-game series, both are under .500 and on the bubble of grabbing the final wild-card spot with a month to go in the regular season. Their seasonlong struggles have created a wide-open race for the pennant in the American League. After having won 77 games all last season, the Tampa Bay Rays (79-54) are in first place, with New York (75-57) right behind, even though Yankees star Aaron Judge hasn’t played since he injured a rib in late April. The Boston Red Sox (73-60), despite having fired most of their coaching staff only weeks into the season, have the third-best record. Most surprising of all are the Chicago White Sox, who are 70-63 only two seasons after they won just 41 games. Trying to keep up are seven teams that are within six games of .500 — including Toronto and Seattle. Each got here in part because of offenses in steep decline. Last season, both ranked in the top five in the American League in runs scored, walks, on-base percentage and slugging percentage. This season, the Blue Jays have drawn the fewest walks in the AL and have the league’s worst on-base percentage, a category in which the Mariners rank fourth worst. They rank third and fourth worst in slugging percentage. Last year, both teams comfortably outscored their opponents; this year, each has a negative run difference. Schneider, the Blue Jays’ manager, sensed trouble brewing immediately as the season began. Routine miscues, including in routine actions like tagging up and fielding bunts, sank the team to an inauspicious 4-4 start. “We’re eight games into the season, and I feel like we’ve had some games that scream ‘not us,’” Schneider told reporters April 4. “And when we play ‘us,’ we’re good.” But Toronto has rarely been good this season, even though Dylan Cease has become a Cy Young Award candidate as one of the best pitchers in the league, allowing only nine home runs and a .175 average. By July 20, as the team fell eight games under .500, Schneider said he shared players’ frustration. “I’m frustrated with them,” he said. “I’m not mad at them.” The most puzzling element of Toronto’s slide is the lack of power from superstar hitter Vladimir Guerrero Jr. Last fall, his eight home runs in just 18 playoff games pushed the Blue Jays into their first World Series since 1993 and to the brink of a title. By this week, however, Guerrero had homered only seven times in 117 games, including none at home. “I lose sleep ... and we need to do a better job,” Ross Atkins, Toronto’s executive vice president and general manager, said this month in a radio appearance about Guerrero’s season. “It has been very disappointing that we haven’t been able to provide the right support for him and the right feedback loop that is correcting this challenge right now.” “To point to exactly what’s happening, listen, yes, we have an understanding of some of the differences. Whether they’re biomechanical, play and approach, there are some subtle differences. There’s no glaring, alarming concern. ... Once those small differences start to become patterns, retraining them while you’re trying to maintain confidence is a very difficult thing.” A rash of injuries has rarely allowed the Mariners to field the lineup they expected for more than a couple of weeks; in one case, infielder Brendan Donovan sustained a concussion practicing in a batting cage. But those who are on the field have struggled mightily, as well, with no one more prominent than Cal Raleigh. His 60 home runs last season obliterated the previous single-season catcher home run record of 48 as the “Big Dumper” became a sensation and came within a few votes of winning the AL Most Valuable Player award. This season, he has hit just 18 home runs as his batting average, on-base percentage and slugging percentage have all cratered to levels well below his career averages. Nearly half the balls he hit last season were hit “hard,” by Baseball Reference’s metric. This season, that rate is down to 37%. “It starts with me; I’m awful. It is what it is,” Raleigh said Aug. 11 after a loss to the Yankees. “I have to find a way to be better and help the guys along. We just have to play better, ultimately.” Raleigh has begun to find answers, homering in four consecutive at-bats in late August. In a sign of just how jumbled the American League has been this season, the Blue Jays and the Mariners aren’t yet out of the race for the postseason, with both three games behind the final wild-card spot. The question is whether they can recapture last season’s magic to actually do it. CORRECTION (Aug. 28, 2026, 11:52 a.m. ET): A previous version of this article misidentified the second team in the subheadline. It’s the Toronto Blue Jays, not the Tampa Bay Rays.

articles.title: MLB's Historically Bad AL West is Also…Dangerous?
articles.summary: This is not the best of times in the American League West. Nobody is having a good time, and the only hope of reprieve lies in October.
articles.body:
This is not the best of times in the American League West. Nobody is having a good time, and the only hope of reprieve lies in October.

At least one team from the AL West will be present in the postseason, and that potential lone entry could make history. As of Thursday, all five teams in the division had a losing record.

The only team to come close to winning a division with a losing record was the 2005 San Diego Padres, who won the NL West at 82-80 and with a minus-42 run differential. Presently, the AL West can only aspire to that level of competence:

It's no wonder three of the five front office heads who began the year in the AL West have lost their jobs. Perry Minasian, David Forst and Dana Brown must have felt like Andy Dufresne escaping Shawshank Penitentiary when they finally got out.

How things went so wrong is a good question. Another good one is whether there's any hope for the AL West.

The AL West produced pennant winners in 2017, 2019, 2021, 2022 and 2023, and came very close to doing so again just last year. This is not a lightweight division. At least, it's not supposed to be.

The reality coming into 2026 was always more complicated. Preseason projections generally painted a picture of a mediocre American League, to the point that even the best team in the AL West (the Mariners, according to FanGraphs ) would have been projected as the fourth-best team in the National League.

Cut to now, and it's impossible to tell the story of what's gone wrong in the AL West without breaking down what's gone wrong with the Mariners.

They have gone from having a top-10 run-scoring offense in 2025 to ranking dead last in MLB in runs scored in 2026.

There's no separating that from the downfalls of Cal Raleigh and Julio Rodríguez . In 2025, they combined for 92 home runs and 13.8 rWAR. With a month left in 2026, they're at 38 home runs and 3.1 rWAR.

Another major problem is a bullpen with a bottom-10 ERA. Ditto for disappointing returns from offseason additions like Josh Naylor and Brendan Donovan , the weirdly inconsistent starting pitching, the… well, the phrase "total system failure" comes to mind with Seattle.

Otherwise, here's the short version for the other teams in the AL West:

Houston Astros: It's hard to win games with an injury-riddled starting rotation that also has a 5.14 ERA.

Texas Rangers: The offense has been cold all year and not one of their top starting pitchers has an ERA under 4.00.

Athletics: An AL-worst 5.48 ERA has made it impossible for them to cover for an offense that has been decimated by injuries.

Los Angeles Angels: The pitching is dreadful, the offense is mediocre, and the result has been exactly what you'd expect.

This is the uncomplicated version. It's also as complicated as it needs to be. Save for the Mariners, the bar in the AL West was set pretty low. Just because they have sunk does not mean a rising tide has come to lift everyone else.

All It Takes Is One AL West Team to Get Hot

Even despite all of the above, we're still living in a world where all three AL West contenders have about the same odds of winning the AL pennant as the league's current No. 2 seed.

The Astros and Rangers are only 3.5 and 4.5 games, respectively, off the pace set by the Chicago White Sox. For now, both Texas clubs share the advantage of upward mobility.

Since hitting a nadir at 11 games under .500 on May 20, the Astros have the third-best record in the AL at 47-36. When all else fails, they have the home run ball to fall back on. They have hit 179 of them, the third-most in MLB.

Since falling six games under .500 on May 28, the Rangers have the AL's fifth-best record at 41-37. The jury's out on Nathan Eovaldi , but they're due to get Josh Jung and Jack Leiter back as reinforcements soon.

This leaves the Mariners as the only one of the three remaining AL West contenders without some measure of top-five aura. Yet they do have one major advantage.

Seen the Mariners' remaining schedule? It makes a cat's naptime look grueling.

Their remaining opponents have a combined .436 winning percentage, largely because they have 17 games left against the teams with the three worst records in MLB. It's the easiest remaining schedule.

The Mariners are already perking up, with wins in eight out of their last 13. All of those are against contenders, so any sustained mojo they can derive from this run should be doubly useful when the pushovers come in September.

Why the AL West Could Surprise People in October

Welcome to the "So you're telling me there's a chance" portion of this program, in which we reassure everyone that even mediocre teams can rise to greatness in the postseason.

Those 2005 Padres didn't win the World Series, but an 83-win St. Louis Cardinals team did just a year later in 2006. They're one of five World Series winners that didn't reach 90 wins, a group that also includes the 2021 Atlanta Braves.

This is relevant to the AL West. The three remaining contenders may be limping to the finish line, but they may have teeth to bear come October.

Nobody wants to face Yordan Alvarez in October. He leads the AL in basically everything, including all three Triple Crown categories with a .319 average, 36 home runs and 91 RBI. He also has a .944 OPS and a World Series-winning homer among his playoff credentials.

Jose Altuve and ( soon enough ) Carlos Correa will be there, too. They have 45 career playoff home runs between them. 'Nuff said.

As suspect as Houston's pitching may be, at least Hunter Brown is rolling with a 2.88 ERA in his last six starts. They also have an elite bullpen trio, with Josh Hader , Bryan Abreu and Steven Okert combining for a 1.30 ERA in the second half.

Even if Jacob deGrom and MacKenzie Gore have ERAs over 4.00, nobody's racing to the bat rack to face either one of them.

Even an aging deGrom, 38, is still fanning 11.0 batters per nine innings, and Gore isn't far behind at 9.9 per nine innings.

Despite their struggles to score runs, you might also be surprised that the Rangers rank third in MLB with a 108 OPS+. It's not an easy lineup to navigate, consisting of as many as six above-average hitters on a good day.

There's also the Corey Seager factor. He's a two-time World Series champ with 19 career playoff home runs. Don't look now, but he's batting .318 with an .884 OPS since returning from his most recent IL stint on July 31.

Seattle's offense has finally been showing signs of life, and that's in part because Raleigh has finally woken up. A little swing adjustment and, BOOM , "Big Dumper" goes off for five home runs and eight RBI in a six-game homestand.

A hot Raleigh is a threat. The same goes for a hot J-Rod, a hot Naylor, and a hot Donovan. If the Mariners get even a couple of those guys getting warm in addition to more of the same from erstwhile ALCS MVP Randy Arozarena , nobody will want to face their offense.

As much as Seattle's bullpen stinks now, it stands to benefit from whatever the rotation loses in October. Maybe it's Bryan Woo , Bryce Miller or Emerson Hancock joining Andrés Muñoz . Or, maybe it's Kade Anderson or even Ryan Sloan , the latter of whom might be the one pitching prospect in MLB with an even higher ceiling than Anderson's.

Perhaps this comes across as a noble, yet pointless effort to put lipstick on the most grotesque sow that MLB's divisional era has ever known. In which case… yeah, you've caught me ruby-red-handed.

At least on the American League side, though, it's a good year for an underdog story. There is no dominant team to act as a gatekeeper for the World Series. Heck, the AL has as many teams playing .550 ball as the NL has playing .600 ball. There are winnable leagues and winnable leagues , and the AL is the latter.

To count out the AL West might be logical, but it is not wise. Remember, the only lasting truth in baseball is that stranger things have happened.

Stats courtesy of Baseball Reference , FanGraphs and Baseball Savant .

articles.title: MLB Report Cards for Every Team With 1 Month to Go
articles.summary: With school starting back up around the country, there is no time like the present for some report card grades on every Major League Baseball team's 2026 season.
articles.body:
With school starting back up around the country, there is no time like the present for some report card grades on every Major League Baseball team's 2026 season.

To be clear from the outset, each team's grade is entirely based on how its winning percentage compares to its preseason win total.

For instance, if both the Dodgers (103.5 preseason win total) and the Rockies (55.5 preseason win total) were sitting at .500—they aren't, but just go with it—the Dodgers would get a big, fat F while the Rockies would be given an A+.

For each team, we'll discuss a pleasant surprise, as well as a sizable disappointment.

Where appropriate, the analysis will focus on how well (or poorly) the team has been playing as of late, but, again, these grades are for the full season and are based on how good the team was supposed to be .

Despite specifying that twice, we're probably about to make some Red Sox and Dodgers fans very angry.

Statistics and records are current through the start of play on Thursday, August 27.

ARI | ATH | ATL | BAL | BOS | CHC | CIN | CLE | COL | CWS | DET | HOU | KC | LAA | LAD | MIA | MIL | MIN | NYM | NYY | PHI | PIT | SD | SEA | SF | STL | TB | TEX | TOR | WSH

Pleasant Surprise : LHP Eduardo Rodríguez

For the first month of the season, the correct answer here would have been Ildemaro Vargas. But while Vargas has a .562 OPS since early May, Rodríguez has continued to shove as the ace of this staff. After successive years with an ERA just north of 5.00, he has it all the way down to 2.50 this year after back-to-back scoreless outings. It's what the Diamondbacks were hoping for when they signed him during the 2023-24 offseason. It just took a while to happen.

Last year was a dud for Gallen, but he did finish strong with a 3.32 ERA over his final 11 starts—virtually identical to his 3.34 ERA from 2020-24. Hard to blame the Snakes for betting on a bounce-back year from their former ace, but Gallen has gone from dud to disaster, presently on the 60-day IL with a 6.34 ERA.

The Diamondbacks are hanging tight in the NL wild-card race, still hoping to get Corbin Burnes back on the mound before the season ends. Nolan Arenado looked hopelessly washed up for the first couple of weeks, but he is tied for the team lead with 21 home runs. Could he be the reason they sneak into October?

Preseason Over/Under : 75.5 wins Current Trajectory : 64.1 wins Recent Returns : 15-43 since June 20

The 22-year-old Bolte wasn't even one of the Athletics' top five prospects coming into the season, but he relentlessly mashed his way through Triple-A with a 1.076 OPS (and 17 stolen bases) in 37 games played before getting the call to the majors. Though he hasn't been anywhere near that potent, he has been a solid, everyday player and an unexpected potential building block for the future.

We Were Expecting More : DH Brent Rooker

Over the past three seasons, Rooker had an .853 OPS, averaging 33 home runs and 90 RBI per year. This season was a much different story, limited by injuries to just 48 games and posting an OPS of .670. Fingers crossed that he comes back in 2027 from his knee surgery as good as new.

Things started out so promising for the A's, who were sitting at 38-38 at roughly the midpoint of their schedule. But the wheels came off in a hurry, as injuries ravaged the lineup while the pitching staff devolved from "not great" to "big yikes." Over the past two months, they've been almost as bad as they were at their lowest point during the (evidently still ongoing) rebuild.

Preseason Over/Under : 86.5 wins Current Trajectory : 95.0 wins Recent Returns : 8-10 since August 7

The surprise here isn't that Dubón has provided value as a versatile defender and a respectable hitter. He also did that in each of the last three seasons with the Astros. Rather, the surprise is how indispensable he has become for Atlanta, even (for some reason) batting cleanup on both Tuesday and Wednesday against the Dodgers. Not bad for a guy who Houston decided wasn't worth paying in his final year of arbitration.

We Were Expecting More : SS Ha-Seong Kim

For one brief moment on Wednesday night, Kim was worth his $20M salary, delivering the walk-off hit in a pivotal win over the Dodgers. Prior to that, however, he had an almost impossibly bad .230 OPS for the year, and he still hasn't had an extra base hit in 2026. He missed the first six weeks of the season with a finger injury, and then had just one single in his next 45 at-bats.

This was an A++ grade back in early June when the Braves had the best record in baseball at 45-21, but they have been sputtering in place for nearly three months at this point. The starting rotation has turned quite a corner in recent weeks, but now the lineup is as riddled with black holes as it was throughout June. Can they hang on and win the NL East?

Preseason Over/Under : 85.5 wins Current Trajectory : 79.1 wins Recent Returns : 11-12 since August 1

After making 12 starts with a 6.24 ERA in 2025, Young wasn't supposed to be part of the equation here. But between Zach Eflin immediately suffering a season-ending injury and Dean Kremer making just two appearances in the first three months, the O's pretty much had to ride with Young. Lo and behold, he has been one of their best pitchers, making 22 starts with a 3.50 ERA.

We Were Expecting More : SS Gunnar Henderson

Henderson has 20 home runs, which is better than last year's total of 17, but he simply has not been the same hitter that he used to be. He had a 155 OPS+ two years ago. Now, he's below league-average with a mark of 95.

After an aggressive offseason headlined by the signings of Pete Alonso and Chris Bassitt and the acquisitions of Shane Baz and Taylor Ward via trade, the Orioles were supposed to bounce back in a big way from last year's 75-87 disappointment. That hasn't been the case, even though the Polar Bear has had a great first year with them. There's still hope for a spot in the postseason, though, if they can finish with a flourish.

Preseason Over/Under : 87.5 wins Current Trajectory : 88.9 wins Recent Returns : 18-9 since July 29

When the Red Sox acquired Bennett from the Nationals for Luis Perales in mid-December, there was no good reason to believe he would be pitching in the majors this season. But a litany of injuries paved the way and this rookie southpaw has made the most of his opportunity. He has come back to earth a bit in August, but he has made 15 starts with a 3.49 ERA.

We Were Expecting More : LHP Garrett Crochet

Strong cases could also be made for Roman Anthony and Jarren Duran, but Crochet was neck-and-neck with Tarik Skubal for last year's AL Cy Young and was expected to be right there again this year. Instead, he had a 6.30 ERA in six starts and hasn't been seen since April due to a shoulder injury.

It's a laughable grade if you happen to have forgotten that we're grading the entire season or that the Red Sox started out 32-46. They've been the best team in baseball since late June, but it has taken those two months of sheer dominance to get them back on track to reach their preseason win total.

Preseason Over/Under : 88.5 wins Current Trajectory : 91.9 wins Recent Returns : 5-8 since August 13

Pleasant Surprise : CF Pete Crow-Armstrong

Surely, PCA was expected to be good, but not "front runner for NL MVP good." He finished ninth in last year's NL MVP race with 31 home runs and 35 stolen bases. However, he limped to the finish line with a .585 OPS over his final 50 games, ending the year at a mark of .768. Now, he's at .924, battling Shohei Ohtani and James Wood for the best OPS in the NL, with a realistic shot at a 40/40 campaign.

We Were Expecting More : RHP Edward Cabrera

The Cubs gave up top prospect Owen Caissie (and more) to acquire Cabrera in January, banking on him becoming a reliable staple in the middle of this rotation. Though initial returns were promising, he has an 8.57 ERA and three separate trips to the IL since early May. (At least he has made 15 starts, though. The Cubs were also expecting more than two appearances from Cade Horton, as well as Justin Steele pitching at some point.)

The Cubs went 7-22 from May 9 to June 10, but they have otherwise been the best team in baseball at 69-36. Similar to the Red Sox, though, that rough patch still counts in this exercise for a team that is marginally ahead of schedule over the course of the full season. If the improved pitching over the past month is for real, look out.

Preseason Over/Under : 67.5 wins Current Trajectory : 85.3 wins Recent Returns : 25-24 since July 1

Detroit's Kevin McGonigle is going to win AL Rookie of the Year, but Peters could be the first runner-up in that vote. Not too shabby for a guy who was playing with the Savannah Bananas five years ago and who was traded for "cash or a player to be named later" eight months ago. Peters hit for the cycle shortly before the All-Star Break and this week has homered in five consecutive games.

We Were Expecting More : RHP Shane Smith

As a rookie in 2025, Smith made 29 starts with a 3.81 ERA. He was arguably the MVP of the White Sox, and the only one selected to represent them at the All-Star Game. If you had told us five months ago that he would make just three appearances with a 10.80 ERA, Chicago having a winning record right now would have been even more inconceivable.

Save for going 18-10 in May, the White Sox have just been hanging around as a .500 team, never much feeling like a serious threat to do damage in October, even as the rest of the AL Central and the AL West keeps propping them up for a first-round bye. But even "hanging around as a .500 team" is better than pretty much anyone expected from this squad after three consecutive seasons with at least 100 losses.

Preseason Over/Under : 80.5 wins Current Trajectory : 76.2 wins Recent Returns : 7-13 since August 7

In the olden days before Wins Above Replacement became the be-all end-all for awards debates, Stewart would be running away with NL ROY. He has 28 home runs, 12 stolen bases, an .806 OPS and an MLB-best 100 RBI. Stewart showed a lot of promise for his couple of weeks in the majors at the end of last season, but no one saw this coming.

We Were Expecting More : RF Noelvi Marté

There was a stretch of nearly two months last summer/fall in which it looked like Marté had finally arrived. The former top prospect had an OPS of nearly .900 during a 47-game run, which included switching from third base to right field. But in 63 games played this year, he has a .550 OPS and was recently sent back to Triple-A.

Early on, the Reds were the kings of one-run games, ending April in sole possession of first place in the NL Central. Since then, however, they've gone 43-60 with the lowest scoring offense in the National League. Stewart and Chase Burns have blossomed into stars worth building around, but the Reds have a lot of holes to fill this winter.

Preseason Over/Under : 79.5 wins Current Trajectory : 82.2 wins Recent Returns : 9-2 since August 15

Messick made a solid first impression last season, posting a 2.72 ERA in seven starts over the final six weeks. But he barely made the cut for the Opening Day rotation, serving as Cleveland's No. 5 starter before blossoming into one of their All-Stars. He has made 26 starts with a 2.50 ERA, 1.01 WHIP and 9.1 K/9.

We Were Expecting More : LHP Logan Allen

Allen was one of the staples of Cleveland's rotation in 2025, making 73 big league starts over the past three seasons. But after a horrific run through spring training (10.0 IP, 20 ER), he was the odd man out of this group, making just one appearance in the Guardians' first 98 games. (He is presently back in the bigs as one of their middle relievers, though.)

Things were looking bleak two weeks ago, but the Guardians made the most of their nine consecutive games against the Giants, Rockies and Angels, vaulting back into sole possession of the AL's final wild card spot. We shall see if it's the beginning of one of their patented strong finishes or just a blip where they happened to find some offense for a change against bad teams.

Preseason Over/Under : 55.5 wins Current Trajectory : 63.3 wins Recent Returns : 14-26 since July 8

Though Rumfield hit pretty well over the past two seasons in the Yankees farm system, it was unlikely he would ever factor into their big league equation. So they shipped him to the Rocky Mountains in late January, where he has blossomed into arguably the second-best player on the team. That he has an OPS of at least .800 both home and away might be his most noteworthy feat.

We Were Expecting More : SS Ezequiel Tovar

Aside from that hopelessly bad Kris Bryant contract, Tovar is the one player with whom the Rockies have a financially substantial contract. But in year No. 3 of that seven-year, $63.5M deal, things are looking grim. Tovar went from 26 home runs and 45 doubles in 2024 to a .602 OPS this season. That's after an impressive run over the past few weeks, too. He was down in the mid-.500s in early August.

It's funny/sad that the second-worst record and the second-worst run differential in the majors is good enough to classify Colorado as better than anticipated. The Rockies might be able to avoid a fourth consecutive season with at least 100 losses, but it is definitely going to be an eighth straight year with a winning percentage of .460 or worse. And yet, any preseason bets on "Colorado over 55.5 wins" will be paying out pretty soon.

Kevin McGonigle has been the rookie star in Detroit, but that's hardly a surprise, coming from the top prospect who signed an eight-year, $150M deal. Melton's dominance, though, has definitely been unexpected. Since missing the first two months with an elbow injury, he has made 16 starts with a 1.86 ERA.

We Were Expecting More : LHP Framber Valdez

Half of Valdez's 26 appearances have been quality starts, including four of his first five after signing with the Tigers. But seemingly every time they've needed him to twirl a gem to stop the bleeding, he has turned in a dud. While his 4.35 ERA isn't exactly dreadful, it's nowhere close to what Detroit had in mind when it made Valdez the highest-paid pitcher in the American League.

Remove the 6-22 record from May, and the Tigers would be 56-49 with a plus-118 run differential—good enough for the AL's No. 2 seed. Instead, they sit nine games below .500, a massive disappointment that prompted the club to trade two quality arms, Tarik Skubal and Casey Mize.

After posting a 5.51 ERA with the Rockies from 2023 to 2024, Lambert spent last season in Japan, where he had a 3.98 ERA. He ended up with the Astros on a minor league deal and only got called up in mid-April after Hunter Brown, Cristian Javier and Tatsuya Imai all landed on the IL. But look at Lambert now, leading the team in innings pitched by a sizable margin, and with a solid 3.66 ERA.

Credit where it's due: Altuve is still providing some value in his age-36 season. Not many second basemen in MLB history can say that. But his play has declined for a third consecutive season. (And this is only year No. 2 of the five-year extension he signed in 2024.)

With Yordan Alvarez chasing a triple crown, the Astros really ought to be running away with what has been a pathetic AL West. But with few exceptions, the starting rotation has been a season-long mess, rated by FanGraphs as the worst in the majors. That's not an easy hurdle to overcome.

Got to love it when a journeyman suddenly has a moment in the sun. Dobnak had logged just 15.0 innings in the majors from 2022-25 with the Twins and spent the first couple months of this season at Seattle's Triple-A affiliate before the Royals purchased him from the Mariners. Since getting called up in early July, the 31-year-old has logged 51.2 innings across 10 appearances with a 1.92 ERA.

Cole Ragans was supposed to be the ace of this staff, but he made eight mostly underwhelming starts before undergoing season-ending UCL surgery. Maikel Garcia, Vinnie Pasquantino and Jonathan India were supposed to be major pieces of Bobby Witt Jr.'s supporting cast, but they've missed a combined total of 224 games. Even Witt missed about three weeks, which damaged his case for AL MVP. The injury bug eventually comes for everyone, but it hit KC hard this year.

The recent nine-game winning streak almost spared the Royals from a failing grade. However, it did little to change the larger picture for a team that had been 24 games below .500 and flirting with the worst record in baseball. With so many key players missing significant chunks of the season, the Royals simply could not stay afloat.

Preseason Over/Under : 70.5 wins Current Trajectory : 62.9 wins Recent Returns : 11-21 since July 22

A rookie who wasn't one of the Angels' top prospects, Ureña started out the year as a middle reliever, spent a couple of weeks down at Triple-A and then came back as a budding ace out of nowhere. Since returning in late April, he has made 22 starts with a 2.98 ERA. He's one behind Reid Detmers for the team lead in quality starts and just might be the long-awaited young arm they can start to build around.

We Were Expecting More : LHP Yusei Kikuchi

An All-Star just last season, Kikuchi was supposed to be one of the stalwarts of this rotation. However, after seven sub-par starts (5.81 ERA), he landed on the IL for nearly four months before finally returning this past Sunday—and struggling again. He was never going to be enough to save their season, but he could've at least helped make things a little more respectable.

It speaks volumes to the current state of this franchise that the Angels have the worst record in the American League and they aren't all that far off from preseason expectations. It was an entertaining first month between José Soriano blossoming into a star and Mike Trout looking like his old self for a change. They still found their way back into the AL West basement, though.

Preseason Over/Under : 103.5 wins Current Trajectory : 97.4 wins Recent Returns : 11-6 since August 8

Pleasant Surprise : LHP Justin Wrobleski

Had the Dodgers' rotation been at full strength throughout the season, it's very likely Wrobleski never would have started a game. But that hypothetical lasted about five minutes, with this southpaw entering the fray in Game No. 10. Over the course of his next 16 appearances, he had a 2.45 ERA and an 11-2 record, becoming a most unexpected All-Star.

Even disregarding the fact that the Dodgers gave him a preposterous $60M AAV on a four-year deal, Tucker has been a shell of his former self. His worst OPS over the past seven seasons was an .808 mark in 2022, when he still accumulated 30 home runs, 107 RBI and 25 stolen bases. He's currently at a .680 OPS, on pace for maybe 15 home runs and 10 stolen bases.

It's a harsh grade for the second-best record in baseball, but can you honestly say the Dodgers have been as good as you thought they'd be? After adding Kyle Tucker and Edwin Díaz to a back-to-back World Series winning roster, the Dodgers really ought to have been able to moonwalk their way to home-field advantage throughout the postseason. But, as has been the case in each of the past two seasons, they hit quite a rough patch in July/August.

Lopez had been one of Miami's more valuable position players over the past two seasons, but mostly because of his value added on defense while posting a .680 OPS. This year, he has one of the top batting averages in all of baseball and an OPS of nearly .800. If Luis Arraez had gotten traded across league lines, Lopez would be the front runner for the NL batting crown right now.

We Were Expecting More : RHP Pete Fairbanks

The Marlins are paying more than $4 million to only three players this season: Sandy Alcantara ($17 million), Pete Fairbanks ($13.3 million) and $10 million of Giancarlo Stanton's salary, retained from the trade eight years ago. Stanton arguably has provided more value to Miami than Fairbanks, who owns a 6.06 ERA and returned to the IL this week.

Not much was expected from the Marlins, who traded away both Edward Cabrera and Ryan Weathers in the span of a week over the offseason. But theirs has been a tale of three seasons: eight games below .500 through the end of May, 26-8 for the next six weeks and eight games below .500 since.

Preseason Over/Under : 84.5 wins Current Trajectory : 99.9 wins Recent Returns : 23-14 since All-Star Break

Milwaukee ranking dead last in the majors in home runs has become an inescapable narrative, but Bauers is doing his best to shoulder the load. His previous career high was 12 home runs, entering 2026 with a career OPS of .672. He enters the home stretch sitting at 23 and .884, respectively.

We Were Expecting More : DH Christian Yelich

The 2018 NL MVP is definitely in the back nine of his career at this point, but Yelich was the star of this lineup just one year ago, giving the Brewers 29 home runs and 103 RBI. He has just nine home runs in 93 games played this season, though, currently with a sub-.700 OPS for what would be the first time in his career. (Knowing this makes it even more absurd that Milwaukee ranks third in the majors in runs scored.)

The Brewers set a franchise record with 97 wins last season and are on pace for slightly more than that this year. But, per usual, they were underestimated in the offseason after losing what had been one of the most important players on their roster. One of these years, we'll learn.

After trading away basically the entire bullpen at last year's deadline, the Twins entered this season with a great big question mark at closer. Even two months into the season, they had 14 saves divvied up among 11 relievers, none of whom had more than two. They finally handed the reins to Gómez, though, about a month after they acquired him from the Rays in late April. He has yet to blow a save in 25 chances (19 saves, six holds) and had a 1.85 ERA through his first 44 appearances.

We Were Expecting More : RHP Simeon Woods Richardson

Over the previous two seasons, Woods Richardson logged 245.0 innings with a 4.11 ERA. And with Pablo López lost for the year early in spring training, he was the clear No. 4 in this rotation heading into the season. He pitched his way right out of a job, though, with a 7.74 ERA in his 12 appearances before Minnesota designated him for assignment. (Making matters worse for the Twins, he has since made seven relief appearances for the Blue Jays with a 1.04 ERA.)

Minnesota entered August with a winning record and elected to do some buying at the trade deadline, adding Dean Kremer, Jeff Hoffman and A.J. Minter. Unfortunately, the Twins have cratered since then and are going to need to flip the script immediately to salvage a wild card spot. Hosting Cleveland from Sept. 11-13 looms extremely large.

Preseason Over/Under : 90.5 wins Current Trajectory : 73.1 wins Recent Returns : 17-11 since July 26

In Ewing, Carson Benge and Nolan McLean, the Mets have had three solid rookies throughout this mess of a season. But while Benge was starting on Opening Day and McLean was the preseason favorite for NL ROY, Ewing kind of came out of nowhere; a mid-May Hail Mary by a team that was both banged up and 10 games below .500. But he has started darn near every game since and become a major asset in the field and on the basepaths.

Plenty of options here, ranging from Marcus Semien and Bo Bichette to Freddy Peralta, Devin Williams and Kodai Senga. But we'll go with the tandem of Jorge Polanco and Mark Vientos as the most glaring source of the Mets' downfall. They were plans A and B at first base after letting Pete Alonso walk in free agency. And whether you like FanGraphs or Baseball-Reference for wins above replacement, that duo has been worth a combined minus-2.5 WAR.

The Mets have been kind of hot over the past month, but it's far too little, far too late. That 12-game losing streak in April doomed them to a summer of misery before the season had really begun. While the Dodgers are breaking baseball with their spending, the Mets have been a reminder that money can't buy happiness.

Preseason Over/Under : 90.5 wins Current Trajectory : 92.0 wins Recent Returns : 25-15 since July 8

Most of the "pleasant surprise" pitchers in this article weren't expected to be regulars in the rotation in 2026. That's not the case with Schlittler, who started in New York's second game of the season and was supposed to be part of this rotation's big four (if it ever got healthy). Becoming the clear ace of this staff and the front runner for AL Cy Young, however, wasn't in the forecast.

At .264, at least Wells is hitting above the Mendoza Line thus far in August. That's the first month this season we've been able to say that, with things getting particularly grim in June when he went 2-for-33 at the dish. Among the 233 players who have made at least 300 plate appearances this season, only Washington's Nasim Nuñez has a lower OPS than Wells' mark of .578.

If you bet on the Yankees win total before the season began, have fun sweating this one out until quite possibly the final game of the year. Though it's a surprise that they are looking up at the Rays in the AL East standings, the Bronx Bombers are almost exactly on pace for 90.5 wins, even though Aaron Judge hasn't played in nearly three months.

Preseason Over/Under : 89.5 wins Current Trajectory : 89.5 wins Recent Returns : 17-7 since August 1

When Adolis García suffered a season-ending injury in mid-June, the Phillies went out and got Derek Hill from the White Sox. He had a .659 OPS in a part-time role, so the asking price wasn't exactly steep. But he turned his season around in Philadelphia, posting an .837 OPS in his first 32 games before fading a bit in recent weeks.

A career .297 hitter with more than 300 stolen bases and nearly 200 home runs, Turner had been worth at least 2.8 bWAR in each of the past 10 seasons. Just last season, he finished fifth in the NL MVP vote. But he has been a sub-replacement-level player this season, struggling both at the plate and in the field. Even so, he has batted either first or second in 128 of the Phillies' 134 games.

They've taken quite the circuitous path to their expected record, starting 9-19, winning 41 of their next 61 games, sputtering through a 7-14 stretch in July and catching fire again in August. Just like the Yankees, though, if you bet this win total in the preseason, have fun sweating for another month.

Heading into this season, Valdéz wasn't even top 10 in Pittsburgh farm system, per our Joel Reuter . He ended last season at Double-A Altoona with a modest .772 OPS in 51 games played. But after a 1.355 OPS in Fall League, a 1.029 OPS in spring training and an .888 OPS in Triple-A, he got his chance. And in 63 games played, he has 15 home runs and an .898 OPS. It's not difficult to argue that his rookie season has been a bigger success than Konnor Griffin's.

We Were Expecting More : DH Marcell Ozuna

Some sluggers like David Ortiz and Nelson Cruz continue to mash all the way to the age of 40. Others seem to spontaneously combust upon turning 35. Evidently, Ozuna is the latter type, as the Pirates gave him $12M for a .203 batting average and a .612 OPS. He slugged .552 between the 2023 and 2024 seasons, but that feels like ancient history now.

As it turns out, the preseason win totals had a crystal ball centered on the state of Pennsylvania, with the Pirates and Phillies the two teams almost exactly where they "should" be. Pittsburgh was holding strong in the wild card picture, though, until about a month ago when what had been one of the most potent offenses in the league suddenly lost its juice.

If you had given me 15, maybe even 20 guesses six months ago on who would lead the Padres in bWAR this season, Ty France wouldn't have been one of those guesses. And while he may ultimately finish behind at least Fernando Tatis Jr. in that race, he is presently in the lead at a 3.6 bWAR with a .862 OPS. Mighty unexpected from a guy who had given four separate teams a sub-.700 OPS over the previous two seasons.

We Were Expecting More : 3B Manny Machado

Without a doubt, Machado has turned things around over the past two-plus months, posting an .807 OPS in his last 68 games. Had he done that all season long, there never would have been a single complaint here. But he had a .586 OPS in his first 63 games and was the primary fall guy as everyone tried to comprehend how the Padres went from a 29-18 NL West leader to a sub-.500 team with a hapless offense.

The Padres have a knack for figuring things out in late July. They went from a 50-50 start to a 43-19 finish two years ago, then went 35-23 over the final two months of last season. They are doing it again this year: after falling three games below .500 on July 23, they have surged into a wild-card position and own baseball's best record since then. They also could get Joe Musgrove and/or Nick Pivetta back at some point.

Preseason Over/Under : 80.5 wins Current Trajectory : 65.8 wins Recent Returns : 7-17 since July 31

He's no longer on the team, but Arraez was one of the few redeeming qualities of this year's Giants squad. The batting average isn't the surprise, as he's on track to win his fourth batting crown in five years. Rather, after seven years as a clear negative on defense, there's a decent chance he'll win a Gold Glove for his work at second base this season.

We Were Expecting More : C Patrick Bailey

Might as well make both of these picks guys who are no longer on the team, right? Bailey never has been much of a hitter, but his value added behind the plate used to make up for it. However, no amount of elite pitch framing could make up for what was a .396 OPS when they traded him to Cleveland in early May.

After four years of stagnant mediocrity, at least the Giants finally found their way out of no-man's land. Unfortunately, they dug down instead of climbing up, presently with their fifth-worst winning percentage of MLB's World Series era. We'll see if they can avoid 100 losses.

Over the past three seasons, it looked like the No. 6 overall pick in the 2020 draft was never going to be anything more for the Mariners than a stopgap solution when one of the regular starting pitchers got hurt. In 162.2 innings of work, he had a 4.81 ERA, a 5.23 FIP and a 6.0 K/9. This year, however, he has a 3.37 ERA, a 3.82 FIP and an 8.4 K/9, becoming so reliable that the M's were willing to move Luis Castillo ahead of the trade deadline.

The Big Dumper has put on a bit of a show in the past week, including going yard three times in the series opener against the Phillies. Through his first 94 games played, though, he had a .569 OPS, operating at a 162-game pace of 22.4 home runs. Even the pessimists who expected Raleigh to come back to earth after last year's homer-palooza certainly didn't think he would regress this much.

For as disappointing as this season has been for the Mariners, the stage is still set for them to sprint into the postseason as AL West champs. Seventeen of their final 22 games come against either the A's, Angels or Rockies, and the other five are home games against the Astros and Rangers. With the Mariners just 2.5 games out of the AL West lead, failing to salvage the season could prompt significant organizational changes.

Preseason Over/Under : 69.5 wins Current Trajectory : 79.8 wins Recent Returns : 15-23 since July 8

If you had given up hope on Walker amounting to anything, you certainly weren't alone. The former top prospect had gone from good as a rookie to bad to worse over the previous two seasons, managing just 11 home runs and a .595 OPS in 162 games played. Had the Cardinals not entered the year still in rebuilding mode, they might have just thrown in the towel. But the 2026 All-Star has rewarded them for their patience with 27 home runs, 18 stolen bases and an .846 OPS.

We Were Expecting More : CF Victor Scott II

Scott never was going to be a clean-up hitter, but he was at least a serviceable player last season with a .305 on-base percentage, 34 stolen bases and outstanding range in center field. He almost led the Cardinals in wins above replacement . This year, none of those things were true, and he was sent back to Triple-A in early June with a sub-.200 batting average.

Like both the Pirates and the Nationals, the Cardinals have faded out of the NL's postseason conversation over the past 4-6 weeks. That they were ever a factor at all, though, after trading away Sonny Gray, Willson Contreras, Brendan Donovan and Nolan Arenado is mighty impressive.

Preseason Over/Under : 76.5 wins Current Trajectory : 96.2 wins Recent Returns : 5-8 since August 14

Pleasant Surprise : LHP Shane McClanahan

When McClanahan took the mound for Tampa Bay's fifth game of the regular season, it had been 972 days since he last pitched in the majors. He was excellent for his first three seasons in the league, but no one knew what to expect from him this year. Aside from a mildly decreased whiff rate, though, he has picked up right where he left off, giving the Rays a 3.10 ERA and 3.33 FIP—on par with his prior career marks of 3.02 and 3.36, respectively.

We Were Expecting More : IF Carson Williams

From 2023-25, Williams played in 341 minor league games, racking up 66 home runs and 75 stolen bases with an OPS slightly north of .800. And after several years as a consensus top 50 prospect, this was supposed to be the year he broke through in the majors, entering the season as Tampa Bay's starting shortstop. Instead, he is back at Triple-A for the third time in 2026, saddled with a .370 OPS in his 16 games played in the majors

Along with the White Sox, the Rays are one of just two teams that have already surpassed their preseason win total. They've been in a bit of a funk over the past two weeks, but they seem to respond with a hot stretch every time we start to question whether they have the staying power to win the AL East.

Preseason Over/Under : 83.5 wins Current Trajectory : 79.8 wins Recent Returns : 11-16 since July 29

With a tip o' the cap to Ezequiel Durán for becoming Texas' MVP as the utility man extraordinaire, Latz becoming an All-Star closer has been quite the stunning development. He didn't record his first save until the Rangers' 27th game, but he has been lights out since then with 26 saves, a 3-0 record and a 1.79 ERA. Not too shabby for a guy whose only save prior to this season was of the "pitched the final three innings of a blowout" variety.

We Were Expecting More : UTIL Josh Smith

Between 2024 and 2025, Smith was Texas' rock. Despite not having a position to call his own, he batted .254 and led the team with 293 games played. But he fell all the way out of their good graces this year, getting sent down to Triple-A on multiple occasions before getting traded to Toronto for Adam Macko. (Who has also been at Triple-A since then.)

Since the end of May, Texas has been perpetually between three games above .500 and four games below .500, almost stuck in neutral while benefiting from the Astros and Mariners refusing to play any better. The Rangers almost feel destined to finish the season at 81-81. Will that be enough to win this division?

Preseason Over/Under : 88.5 wins Current Trajectory : 78.6 wins Recent Returns : 11-7 since August 7

When Varland first broke into the majors in 2022, he was a starting pitcher, not transitioning fully to the bullpen until last season. He entered 2026 with zero career saves and a 4.66 ERA. But he has become almost indisputably the best closer in the American League, boasting a 1.20 ERA while going 30-for-31 in save opportunities.

We Were Expecting More : 1B Vladimir Guerrero Jr.

In totality, Toronto's offense has been a colossal disappointment, entering play on Wednesday dead last in the majors in runs scored. That isn't entirely Guerrero's fault, but he really has not helped matters with seven home runs and a .687 OPS. It's incomprehensible that he has yet to homer at home this season.

It's probably generous to give Toronto anything other than a failing grade, as they clearly have been a $365M failure up to this point. They aren't quite as far off in their win total trajectory as some teams, though, and there's still hope that they can capitalize on the one-two punch of a favorable remaining schedule and a wide-open race for the AL's final wild card spot.

Griffin had spent the past three seasons in Japan and entered the current campaign with just eight innings pitched in his MLB career. The Nationals brought him in on a one-year, $5.5M deal, which is roughly what the Rockies paid each of Tomoyuki Sugano and Jose Quintana for their services. Nevertheless, he was an All-Star, making 22 starts with a 3.06 ERA before they traded him to Cleveland.

We Were Expecting More : 3B Brady House and OF Dylan Crews

House was Washington's No. 11 overall pick in 2021, while Crews went No. 2 overall in 2023. Although many of Washington's position players have exceeded expectations, those former top prospects have not followed suit. Both have been barely replacement-level players, each with a sub-.300 on-base percentage. Perhaps next year will bring a turnaround.

They've gone belly up over the past month, losing eight of their last nine series while free-falling out of the wild-card picture. Still, though, it's only a question of when they're going to cash this over, as they were drastically better than expected through the first 108 games of virtually unstoppable offense.

articles.title: Little League World Series 2026 Updated US, International Brackets and Schedule
articles.summary: And then there were four.
articles.body:
The United States and International brackets will be decided Friday in Williamsport at the 2026 Little League World Series, with a trip to the tournament's championship game on the line.

Which four teams will compete for the honor and when can viewers check out the action from historic Lamade Stadium?

Mountain Region: Paseo Verde Little League (Henderson, Nevada)

Great Region: West Side Little League (Hamilton, Ohio)

Curaçao Region: Pariba Little League (Willemstad, Curaçao)

Japan: Joto Little League (Tokyo, Japan)

Challenger Division Exhibition Game: Berwyn, Pennsylvania vs. Oakley, California (Not televised)

Game 35 - International Championship: Curaçao Region vs. Japan Region (12:30 p.m., ABC)

Game 36 - United States Championship: Mountain Region vs. Great Lakes Region (3:30 p.m., ABC)

Ohio got a complete game out of pitcher Walker Osborne and a huge bases-clearing triple from Bob Frazier to defeat Iowa, 7-1, and set up a high-stakes showdown with Nevada in the United States Championship Game on Friday.

It was a dominant performance by a team that is tied for the most games played in this year's tournament at six.

Will the extra games prove costly and take their toll on the team as it plays for the right to represent its country in the Little League World Series Championship game? Perhaps, but the squad is battle tested and will look to hang the first "L" on Paseo Verde LL from Henderson, Nevada on Friday afternoon.

Joining Ohio with six games played in this tournament is Japan, who has won four elimination games to set up its rematch with Curaçao in the international final.

In their first meeting, Curaçao blanked the team from Tokyo, beating them decisively, 6-0.

An 11-time winner in the Little League World Series, a victory would bring Japan one closer to Chinese-Taipei, who holds the record for most LLWS victories by an international team with 18.

articles.title: Watch Ex-Mets Star Jose Iglesias Makes Broadway Debut in Trending Video
articles.summary: Two years after "OMG" became a rousing success and an anthem for the New York Mets, Jose Iglesias brought his unique musical ability to the stage.
articles.body:
Two years after "OMG" became a rousing success and an anthem for the New York Mets, Jose Iglesias brought his unique musical ability to the stage.

Iglesias made his Broadway debut on Thursday night during a performance of Buena Vista Social Club .

The former MLB All-Star played the Narrator as part of the show. Buena Vista Social Club debuted off-Broadway in 2023 before opening at the Gerald Schoenfeld Theatre in March 2025.

Iglesias, whose stage name is Candelita, started producing music in 2024 after signing with the Mets. His single "OMG" became a such a hit that MLB had him perform it as part of the festivities at the 2024 Home Run Derby.

articles.summary: Casey Mize faces the Tampa Bay Rays as the San Diego Padres fight for the final Wild Card spot, but his history against Rays hitters is ugly.
articles.body: I ended up going 1-1 yesterday in the two WNBA plays that I put out for the night. Not the end of the world, but I'm glad we have a full slate of baseball games again today for us to choose from. I'm back at it with some really intriguing games tonight. We have Tarik Skubal returning to Detroit for the first time since he was traded, and honestly, I'd probably fade him as it might be pretty emotional. But, I have my eyes set on a different former Tigers hurler as the Padres take on the Rays. The San Diego Padres have been one of the hotter teams in baseball. They are currently sitting at 72-62 and owner of the final Wild Card spot. This team has more than enough talent, but it seems like they haven't been able to put it together for a full season. I still maintain that if they can get it together in the postseason, they have a roster dangerous enough to win the World Series. Sure, you can probably say that about a lot of teams, but I think it is more true of the Padres than the majority of teams simply due to the talent on the roster. New Padres owner Kwanza Jones puts on a performance for the ages at introductory presser As usual, they went out to add more talent at the trade deadline. One of those additions takes the hill tonight, as Casey Mize comes to the mound. He is 5-7 for the season with a 3.44 ERA and a 1.09 WHIP. Mize has struggled on the road a bit more than in his home stadium this season, but the majority of those numbers came when he was with the Tigers. Since coming to San Diego, he has had two strong starts and two awful ones. Rays hitters have rocked Mize in the past, with 12 hits in 29 at-bats, so this could be another ugly one from him. The Tampa Bay Rays are one of the best teams in baseball, and currently own the No. 1 spot in the American League. They probably will be the owner of the spot when the playoffs are finalized. If it isn't them, then it is probably going to be some other American League East team. The Rays would need a complete collapse for them to lose a postseason spot. Based on batting average, this team is the best offensive team in baseball. However, even that success hasn't always translated to runs. The team is at just 17th in the league. The pitching staff has been equally strong for the Rays. They have a 3.78 ERA collectively and a 1.15 WHIP. Throwing today for the Rays is one of their aces, Shane McClanahan. For the season, he is just 9-6, but he owns a 3.10 ERA and a 1.12 WHIP. He has been outstanding at home with a 2.32 ERA and holds opponents to just a .189 batting average. He hasn't allowed more than three earned runs in a start since the middle of July, and in 16 of 22 starts, he has held opponents to two or fewer earned runs. Padres hitters are batting just .197 against him. CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM I bet on McClanahan last time he pitched when he took on the Orioles. He went five strong innings and didn't allow a run. We are going to back him again here, but I'm going just the first five innings. The bullpen let me down last time, and the Orioles won in 10 innings. I'm taking the Rays to win this one, but just through five innings. articles.title: Tarik Skubal Opens Up About Tigers Revenge Game, Reveals His 'True Crime Ritual' After Dodgers Trade
articles.summary: Less than one month after being traded to the Los Angeles Dodgers by the Detroit Tigers, Tarik Skubal will make his first start against his former team at Comerica Park on Friday night.
articles.body:
Less than one month after being traded to the Los Angeles Dodgers by the Detroit Tigers, Tarik Skubal will make his first start against his former team at Comerica Park on Friday night.

Speaking to The Athletic's Fabian Ardaya about his first appearance in Detroit as a visiting player, Skubal cited the "challenge" of trying to keep his emotions in check.

"It's playing baseball in a place that's obviously special to me, right?" Skubal said . "I spent eight years there. But I'm just trying to play baseball. That's gonna be the challenge, just to keep the game the game."

One thing Ardaya noted that helps Skubal maintain some semblance of normalcy, particularly throughout this season as he found himself the subject of trade rumors for months, is a "true crime ritual" that he regularly watches and recently included a Charles Manson documentary on Netflix.

"That was wild," Skubal said of that particular doc.

The left-hander revealed the routine of his day, which includes true-crime docs, is essential to him being able to maintain focus throughout the grind of an MLB season.

"If I let my focus shift from that and I start worrying about what's happening three months from now or what has already happened, it just is a distraction," Skubal said. "That's all it is. So I don't really ever think like that. It does me no good to be in that headspace."

Skubal was part of the Tigers organization from 2018 to '26. He went from a ninth-round draft pick out of Seattle University to becoming a two-time AL Cy Young winner in his last two full seasons in Detroit.

"I'm sure there will be some emotion, obviously," Skubal told Ardaya about how he expects to feel on Friday night. "But at the same time, the game of baseball is normal for me. That's my normal, is playing baseball."

The Tigers made the playoffs in each of the past two years, with their 2024 wild-card berth ending their 10-year playoff drought.

There have been some bumps along the way for Skubal early in his Dodgers tenure, but nothing that should have anyone concerned about his ability to be a dominant pitcher when the postseason starts.

Through his first four starts with Los Angeles, Skubal has a 3.38 ERA with 30 strikeouts over 24.0 innings. He has allowed at least two earned runs in three of those outings.

The Tigers are one of four teams Skubal has never gone up against in his MLB career. He will cross them off the list on Friday at 6:40 p.m. ET.

Friday will mark Skubal's first road start since Aug. 4 when he made his Dodgers debut against the Chicago Cubs at Wrigley Field. The 29-year-old has a 2.67 ERA over 445.2 innings in 77 career starts at Comerica Park.

articles.title: Luis Castillo faces Dean Kremer as White Sox and Twins meet in crucial AL Central series
articles.summary: The Chicago White Sox hold a 2.5-game lead in the American League Central, but Luis Castillo's struggles since arriving from Seattle raise questions.
articles.body: The postseason race is heating up, and I'm here for it. I tend to think that baseball has the best postseason races. I'm not sure that I have a great justification for it, but I'll share my reasoning anyway. The NFL tends to have too many spots locked up too soon. The NBA has too many spots in general, and with essentially 20 teams getting some sort of playoff shot, it's just not interesting. The NHL has a pretty decent race, but the postseason itself for the NHL is more entertaining. With baseball, the trade deadline gets a flurry of moves, and then we see the race. No spot has been locked up yet, but we have a general idea of those with a true chance and those without. The Chicago White Sox may actually pull this off. They are 70-63 for the season, and currently own a 2.5-game lead in the American League Central. However, the vast majority of their success has come at home. They are 29-36 on the road, and maybe that is just a sign of a young team. If you're a pessimistic Sox fan, you look at their road record and the fact that Cleveland is always lurking, and you can't be comfortable. However, the optimist says they are in control of their destiny and playing with house money this season, regardless of what happens. They made their biggest splash in years by acquiring today's starter, Luis Castillo. It is hard to blame them for a lack of moves when the team was a disaster for the past few years, so it was nice to see them adding instead of subtracting. Castillo is having a rough year, though. For the season, he is 4-10 with a 5.19 ERA and a 1.42 WHIP. Since coming over from Seattle, he has allowed 12 earned runs in 18.1 innings. He does have a good track record against the Twins, though. He has allowed them to hit just .228 against him in 123 at-bats. The Minnesota Twins were one of those borderline teams at the deadline. You could've made a case to abandon the season and tell them to look to next year. However, they were in a position where they could also make a run at the division. They ultimately held onto their key pieces despite a lot of interest. The team hasn't been able to find their footing, though, and are now 6.5 games back in the division, and they are 64-70 at the moment. I suppose a series sweep here could go a long way if they want a true shot at the postseason. Twins Promote Top-15 MLB Prospect OF Walker Jenkins To Make Debut vs. White Sox The Twins did make some moves at the deadline, even if they didn't trade away the guys others wanted. They acquired today's starter, Dean Kremer, from the Orioles. For the year, Kremer is just 2-4 with a 5.22 ERA, but he has a strong 1.18 WHIP. Part of the issue is that he has allowed 14 homers in 58.2 innings. So he isn't allowing a ton of baserunners, but when people are hitting him, they are hitting him hard. Almost 30% of the hits he has allowed have left the yard. Sox hitters are batting just .205 against him in 39 at-bats. Essentially, it boils down to the traffic on the basepaths. Kremer allows fewer guys on the bases than Castillo, so I think he gives the Twins a better chance to win games.
