articles.title: MLB's Erik Tolman Opens Up About Amputation Scare, 'My Life Flashed Before My Eyes'
articles.summary: Six days after making his MLB debut, Washington Nationals reliever Erik Tolman opened up about the harrowing incident during a minor league game in 2023 that nearly led to him having part of his leg amputated.
articles.body:
Six days after making his MLB debut, Washington Nationals reliever Erik Tolman opened up about the harrowing incident during a minor league game in 2023 that nearly led to him having part of his leg amputated.

Speaking to The Athletic's Spencer Nusbaum in the wake of his big league debut, Tolman said his "life flashed before my eyes" when thinking back on his in-game injury while playing for the Fredericksburg Nationals.

It occurred on Aug. 2, 2023, in his ninth appearance of the season and sixth for Fredericksburg after having two separate Tommy John surgeries in 2021 and 2022.

Tolman was jogging out to the mound in the third inning when he attempted to skip over the foul line as part of a superstitious ritual many pitchers engage in, except a spike on his cleat got caught in the turf and he landed awkwardly.

Tolman, a 14th-round pick by the Nationals in 2021, told FanGraphs' David Laurila in May that the full extent of damage was a torn ACL, PCL, LCL, hamstring torn off the bone and a ruptured peroneal nerve that caused a foot drop, which caused the foot to be paralyzed for more than a year and nearly resulted in part of his leg being amputated:

"I had surgery to fix it, so now I'm only limited in my mobility. I can only go up and down. I can't go in or out at all, and I still can't feel the top of my foot. I had to teach myself to walk again. I basically had to rewire my brain in order to walk, run, or even drive."

Nusbaum noted Tolman needed three surgeries over an 11-month period, including one that involved moving a muscle from the back of his leg to the front in an attempt to correct his foot drop.

According to Nusbaum, New Year's Day 2025 was a turning point for Tolman when he was able to make a 5.5-hour drive from California to Arizona because it was when he decided he wanted to put himself through the type of rehab that would be required to have a shot at playing baseball again.

"Since I made that decision, I feel like I'm much happier in life," Tolman said. "Nothing but smiles now."

Tolman eventually made it back to pro ball in 2025 when he appeared in 33 games for three different teams in the minors. He started this season in Triple-A and made 32 appearances (one start) before getting called up by the Nationals on Aug. 19.

Tolman made his first MLB appearance on Aug. 22, tossing a scoreless inning against the Miami Marlins. He has thrown a total of 2.2 innings in three appearances, allowing no runs on two hits and two walks with two strikeouts.

The left-hander recorded his first career hold on Thursday in the Nationals' 7-1 win over the Colorado Rockies.

articles.summary: Rookie shortstop George Lombard Jr. has committed errors in six straight games, becoming the first New York Yankees shortstop to do that since 1915.

articles.title: Matt Shaw returns to Cubs after missing 2 months due to hand injury
articles.summary: Shaw's versatility will give manager Craig Counsell options with Dansby Swanson out until late September.
articles.body:
Matt Shaw is back with the Chicago Cubs after missing the past two months with a left-hand sprain.

The 24-year-old infielder/outfielder was reinstated from the injured list Friday as the Cubs open a seven-game homestand beginning with the Cincinnati Reds.

Outfielder Kevin Alcántara was optioned to Triple-A in a corresponding move.

In five rehab games in with Triple-A Iowa, Shaw batted .316 with 6 hits, 4 RBI and 1 stolen base in 19 at-bats. Prior to his injury, he had 20 RBI and 4 home runs while batting .246 through 56 games with the Cubs.

While in Iowa, Shaw saw time at second base, giving Cubs manager Craig Counsell a potential option in the infield. With Dansby Swanson out until at least late September, Nico Hoerner could remain at shortstop while Shaw gets time at second base.

Shaw has seen the bulk of his playing time with the Cubs this season in the outfield. Last season, the No. 13 overall pick in the 2023 MLB draft started 114 games at third base. But the signing of Alex Bregman changed his role.

articles.title: Rays' $2.3B Stadium Deal Approved, Opening Day Teased After City Council Vote
articles.summary: The Tampa Bay Rays' proposed $2.36 billion ballpark deal was approved following a vote by the Hillsborough County Commission on Friday.
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Rays' proposed $2.36 billion ballpark deal was approved following a vote by the Hillsborough County Commission on Friday.

The Tampa City Council also voted to approve the stadium agreement on Thursday.

Per MLB.com's Adam Berry , the team laid out a project schedule in which "substantial completion" of the ballpark will be reached by the end of 2028 before a "final completion" in March 2029 so that it can be ready for Opening Day.

A tentative agreement regarding the stadium was initially finalized in May, with the Rays releasing new renderings of the ballpark just under two months later.

The stadium will be located on Hillsborough College's Dale Mabry campus as part of a mixed-use district and will contain a capacity of approximately 31,000.

The Rays have played at St. Petersburg's Tropicana Field since 1998, but their current lease expires following the 2028 MLB season.

Tampa Bay remains on track to move to its new ballpark in 2029.
